    private static boolean invokeThreshold(int position, Integer total) {
        return (boolean) ReflectionTestUtils.invokeMethod(LearningProgressService.class, "reachesThreshold", position, total);
    }

    private static LearningProgress progress(boolean completed, int position) {
        try {
            Constructor<LearningProgress> ctor = LearningProgress.class.getDeclaredConstructor();
            ctor.setAccessible(true);
            LearningProgress p = ctor.newInstance();
            ReflectionTestUtils.setField(p, "completed", completed);
            ReflectionTestUtils.setField(p, "lastPosition", position);
            return p;
        } catch (ReflectiveOperationException e) {
            throw new IllegalStateException(e);
        }
    }

    private static LessonContextView lesson(String publicationState) {
        return lesson(publicationState, "TEXT", 600);
    }

    /** totalLength = lessons.total_length (V5); 600 cho khá»›p cÃ¡c test cÅ© dÃ¹ng video 600 giÃ¢y. */
    private static LessonContextView lesson(String publicationState, String contentType, Integer totalLength) {
        return new LessonContextView() {
            @Override public Long getLessonId() { return LESSON_ID; }
            @Override public String getLessonTitle() { return "Lesson"; }
            @Override public String getContentType() { return contentType; }
            @Override public Long getCourseId() { return COURSE_ID; }
            @Override public String getCourseTitle() { return "Spring Boot 101"; }
            @Override public String getPublicationState() { return publicationState; }
            @Override public Integer getTotalLength() { return totalLength; }
        };
    }

    private static LessonProgressView lessonRow(Long lessonId, Long completed, Integer position, LocalDateTime accessedAt) {
        return new LessonProgressView() {
            @Override public Long getLessonId() { return lessonId; }
            @Override public String getLessonTitle() { return "Lesson " + lessonId; }
            @Override public String getContentType() { return "VIDEO"; }
            @Override public Long getChapterId() { return 1L; }
            @Override public String getChapterTitle() { return "Chapter"; }
            @Override public Long getCompleted() { return completed; }
            @Override public Integer getLastPosition() { return position; }
            @Override public LocalDateTime getLastAccessedAt() { return accessedAt; }
        };
    }

    @Test
    void student_cannotReadQuizQuestions_beforeStartTime() throws Exception {
        String question = as(LECTURER_OWNER, post("/api/courses/9101/questions").contentType(JSON).content("""
                {"content":"2 + 2?","type":"SINGLE_CHOICE","options":[
                  {"content":"4","correct":true},{"content":"5","correct":false}]}
                """)).andExpect(status().isCreated()).andReturn().getResponse().getContentAsString();
        int questionId = JsonPath.read(question, "$.id");

        // MySQL TIMESTAMP tá»‘i Ä‘a 2038-01-19, nÃªn dÃ¹ng 2037
        String quiz = as(LECTURER_OWNER, post("/api/courses/9101/quizzes").contentType(JSON).content("""
                {"title":"Midterm","startTime":"2037-12-31T08:00:00","endTime":"2037-12-31T09:00:00",
                 "maxAttempts":1,"questions":[{"questionId":%d,"points":1}]}
                """.formatted(questionId))).andExpect(status().isCreated()).andReturn().getResponse().getContentAsString();
        int quizId = JsonPath.read(quiz, "$.quiz.id");
        as(LECTURER_OWNER, post("/api/courses/9101/quizzes/" + quizId + "/publish")).andExpect(status().isOk());

        enroll(STUDENT, 9101);
        as(STUDENT, get("/api/courses/9101/quizzes/" + quizId)).andExpect(status().isForbidden());
    }

    // ================================================================= auth

    /** TÃ i khoáº£n INACTIVE + sai máº­t kháº©u pháº£i tráº£ vá» giá»‘ng há»‡t tÃ i khoáº£n ACTIVE + sai máº­t kháº©u. */
    @Test
    void login_inactiveAccount_isIndistinguishableFromWrongPassword() throws Exception {
        MvcResult active = login("student_a", "wrong-password");
        MvcResult inactive = login("student_b", "wrong-password");

        assertEquals(401, active.getResponse().getStatus());
        assertEquals(active.getResponse().getStatus(), inactive.getResponse().getStatus());
        assertEquals(active.getResponse().getContentAsString(), inactive.getResponse().getContentAsString());
    }

    // ============================================================== helpers

    private ResultActions as(String username, MockHttpServletRequestBuilder request) throws Exception {
        return mvc.perform(request.header("Authorization", token(username)));
    }

    private String token(String username) throws Exception {
        String cached = tokens.get(username);
        if (cached != null) {
            return cached;
        }
        String body = login(username, "123456").getResponse().getContentAsString();
        String token = "Bearer " + JsonPath.<String>read(body, "$.accessToken");
        tokens.put(username, token);
        return token;
    }

    private MvcResult login(String username, String password) throws Exception {
        return mvc.perform(post("/api/auth/login").contentType(JSON)
                .content("{\"username\":\"" + username + "\",\"password\":\"" + password + "\"}"))
                .andReturn();
    }

    private void enroll(String username, int courseId) throws Exception {
        as(username, post("/api/courses/" + courseId + "/enroll")).andExpect(status().isCreated());
    }
}

package com.smartcampus.backend.support;

import com.smartcampus.backend.common.security.UserAccount;
import com.smartcampus.backend.enrollment.entity.Enrollment;
import com.smartcampus.backend.enrollment.entity.EnrollmentStatus;
import com.smartcampus.backend.enrollment.repository.projection.CourseEnrollmentInfo;
import com.smartcampus.backend.enrollment.repository.projection.UserAccountInfo;
import org.springframework.test.util.ReflectionTestUtils;

/** Small builders shared by the unit tests. */
public final class TestData {

    private TestData() {
    }

    public static Enrollment enrollment(Long id, Long studentId, Long courseId, EnrollmentStatus status) {
        Enrollment e = new Enrollment(studentId, courseId);
        ReflectionTestUtils.setField(e, "id", id);
        ReflectionTestUtils.setField(e, "status", status);
        return e;
    }

    public static CourseEnrollmentInfo course(Long id, String title, String publicationState, String window) {
        return new CourseEnrollmentInfo() {
            @Override public Long getId() { return id; }
            @Override public String getTitle() { return title; }
            @Override public String getPublicationState() { return publicationState; }
            @Override public String getEnrollmentWindow() { return window; }
        };
    }

    public static UserAccountInfo userInfo(Long id, String role, String status) {
        return new UserAccountInfo() {
            @Override public Long getId() { return id; }
            @Override public String getRole() { return role; }
            @Override public String getStatus() { return status; }
        };
    }

    public static UserAccount student(Long id) {
        return new UserAccount(id, UserAccount.STUDENT, "ACTIVE", "Student " + id);
    }

    public static UserAccount lecturer(Long id) {
        return new UserAccount(id, UserAccount.LECTURER, "ACTIVE", "Lecturer " + id);
    }

    public static UserAccount admin(Long id) {
        return new UserAccount(id, UserAccount.ADMIN, "ACTIVE", "Admin " + id);
    }
}

package com.smartcampus.backend;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.security.crypto.bcrypt.BCryptPasswordEncoder;

public class PasswordHashTest {

    @Test
    void generateHash() {
        BCryptPasswordEncoder encoder = new BCryptPasswordEncoder();

        String password = "123456";

        String hash = encoder.encode(password);

        System.out.println("BCrypt hash: " + hash);
        System.out.println("Matches: " + encoder.matches(password, hash));

    void everyNewEndpoint_requiresLogin() throws Exception {
        mockMvc.perform(post("/api/courses/9101/withdraw")).andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());

        mockMvc.perform(get("/api/analytics/courses")).andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());
        mockMvc.perform(get("/api/notifications/me")).andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());
    }

    // =============================================================== helpers

    private ResultActions call(String username, MockHttpServletRequestBuilder request) throws Exception {
        return mockMvc.perform(request.with(user(username)));
    }

    private static int id(ResultActions result, String jsonPath) throws Exception {
        Number value = JsonPath.read(result.andReturn().getResponse().getContentAsString(), jsonPath);
        return value.intValue();
    }

    private int count(String sql) {
        Integer value = jdbcTemplate.queryForObject(sql, Integer.class);
        return value == null ? 0 : value;
    }

package com.smartcampus.build;

import com.smartcampus.backend.BackendApplication;
import org.springframework.boot.builder.SpringApplicationBuilder;
import org.springframework.boot.web.server.context.WebServerApplicationContext;
import org.springframework.context.ConfigurableApplicationContext;
import tools.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
import tools.jackson.databind.node.ObjectNode;

import java.net.URI;
import java.net.http.HttpClient;
import java.net.http.HttpRequest;
import java.net.http.HttpResponse;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.time.Duration;

/** Exports the OpenAPI document using the application's test profile. */
public final class OpenApiGenerator {

    private OpenApiGenerator() {
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        if (args.length != 1) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Expected the OpenAPI output path");
        }

        Path output = Path.of(args[0]);
        Files.createDirectories(output.getParent());
        Files.deleteIfExists(output);

        try (ConfigurableApplicationContext context = new SpringApplicationBuilder(BackendApplication.class)
                .profiles("test")
                .run("--server.port=0")) {
            int port = ((WebServerApplicationContext) context).getWebServer().getPort();
            HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(URI.create("http://localhost:" + port + "/v3/api-docs"))
                    .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(30))
                    .GET()
                    .build();
            HttpResponse<String> response = HttpClient.newHttpClient()
                    .send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
            if (response.statusCode() != 200) {
                throw new IllegalStateException("OpenAPI endpoint returned HTTP " + response.statusCode()
                        + ": " + response.body());
            }

            ObjectMapper mapper = new ObjectMapper();
            ObjectNode document = (ObjectNode) mapper.readTree(response.body());
            if (!document.has("openapi") || !document.has("paths")) {
                throw new IllegalStateException("OpenAPI endpoint returned an invalid document");
            }
            document.remove("servers"); // The temporary web server has a different port on every build.
            Files.writeString(output,
                    mapper.writerWithDefaultPrettyPrinter().writeValueAsString(document) + System.lineSeparator(),
                    StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
            System.out.println("Generated OpenAPI: " + output.toAbsolutePath());
        }
    }
}

# Smart Campus - Online Learning Platform

Smart Campus is an online learning platform developed for the CO3103 course project.

The system has three main roles:

- Student
- Lecturer
- Administrator

Advanced component: **Learning Analytics and Early Warning**.

---

## 1. Tech Stack

### Backend
- Java
- Spring Boot
- Spring Data JPA
- MySQL 8.4
- Flyway
- Maven

### Frontend
- React
- TypeScript

### Development
- Docker
- Docker Compose
- GitHub
- GitHub Projects

---

## 2. Project Structure


## 11. Database Migration

Database schema is managed by Flyway.

Migration files:

```text

```

Example:

```text

V2__add_example.sql
V3__update_example.sql
```

### Rules

1. Do not manually modify the shared database schema.
2. Do not modify an existing migration after it has been merged and shared.
3. Create a new migration for every new schema change.
4. Pull the latest `main` before creating a migration to avoid duplicate version numbers.

## 12. Useful Commands

### Run backend tests

The full test suite needs Java 25+ and a running Docker daemon. Start Docker Desktop and verify that Docker is ready:

```bash
docker info
```

From the project root, run:

```bash
cd backend
./mvnw test             # macOS / Linux
```

On Windows, run `mvnw.cmd test` instead. A successful run ends with `BUILD SUCCESS` and `Tests run: 40, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` (the count may grow as tests are added).

#### How the test environment is configured

- `src/test/resources/application-test.yaml` contains the test datasource and a fixed JWT signing secret used only by tests. No local `.env`, `JWT_SECRET`, `DB_URL`, `DB_USERNAME`, or `DB_PASSWORD` is needed for `./mvnw test`.
- Spring integration test classes use `@ActiveProfiles("test")`. Add this annotation to new `@SpringBootTest` classes so they use the isolated test configuration.
- The datasource URL `jdbc:tc:mysql:8.4:///smart_campus_test` tells Testcontainers to start a disposable MySQL 8.4 container. Flyway creates its schema before the tests run. Testcontainers stops the container after the test JVM exits.
- The test database is separate from the development database at `localhost:3306/smart_campus`. You do not need to run `docker compose up` or manually create `smart_campus_test` before testing. Docker Desktop only needs to be running.

If the tests report `Could not find a valid Docker environment`, start Docker Desktop and check `docker info` before retrying. `Access denied for user 'smartcampus'@'localhost'` during a Spring test usually means that test class is missing `@ActiveProfiles("test")` and is using the development datasource.

### Generate OpenAPI

With Docker Desktop running, `./mvnw verify` and `./mvnw install` automatically regenerate `backend/target/openapi.json` (run the commands from `backend/`). During Maven's `integration-test` phase, the generator in `src/test/java` starts the backend on a temporary port with the `test` profile, reads `/v3/api-docs`, writes the file, and closes the application. The existing `springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui` dependency provides that endpoint; the Maven Exec plugin invokes the generator. The generated file is a Maven build artifact and is not committed to Git. `compile` and `test` stop before this phase and do not generate the file.

```bash
cd backend
./mvnw clean verify
```

On Windows, use `mvnw.cmd clean verify`. Docker must be running for the integration tests and OpenAPI generation.

### Other commands

Start MySQL:

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

Stop containers:

```bash
docker compose down
```

Check containers:

```bash
docker compose ps
```

Run backend:

```bash
cd backend
mvnw.cmd spring-boot:run
```

Run frontend:

```bash
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

Update local `main`:

```bash
git checkout main
git pull origin main
```

# Smart Campus â€“ System Specification

## 1. Introduction

### 1.1 Purpose

Smart Campus is an online learning platform designed to support teaching,
learning, assessment, and learning-progress monitoring in a university
environment.

The platform provides lecturers with tools to organize courses and learning
materials, while students can participate in courses, access learning content,
complete assessments, and monitor their learning progress.

In addition to standard Learning Management System (LMS) functionality,
Smart Campus incorporates Learning Analytics and Early Warning capabilities
to help lecturers identify students who may be at risk of falling behind.

### 1.2 Objectives

The main objectives of Smart Campus are to:

- Provide a centralized environment for online teaching and learning.
- Support structured course and learning-content management.
- Allow students to participate in courses and track their learning progress.
- Support assignments, assessments, and learning interactions.
- Collect learning activity data generated during the learning process.
- Transform learning data into meaningful information for lecturers.
- Identify potentially at-risk students and support timely intervention.

---

## 2. System Context

Smart Campus operates as a web-based learning platform.

Students use the platform to participate in courses and learning activities.
Lecturers create and manage courses, deliver learning content, conduct
assessments, and monitor student performance.

Administrators maintain the overall learning environment by managing users,
courses, and system-level information.

During normal system usage, learning activities and assessment results are
recorded. The Learning Analytics component processes this information to
generate risk assessments that assist lecturers in identifying students who
may require additional support.

---

## 3. User Roles

### 3.1 Student

A Student is a learner participating in courses available through the system.

Students interact with learning content, assessments, discussions, and other
learning activities. The system records relevant learning progress and
activity information associated with the student.

### 3.2 Lecturer

A Lecturer is responsible for delivering and managing courses.

Lecturers organize course content, manage learning activities and assessments,
monitor student progress, and use learning analytics information to identify
students who may require intervention.

### 3.3 Administrator

An Administrator is responsible for maintaining the operational environment
of the platform.

Administrators manage users, courses, roles, and system-level information
necessary for the platform to operate correctly.

---

## 4. System Scope

Smart Campus consists of the following major functional areas:

### 4.1 Identity and Access Management

Provides user authentication, authorization, account management, and
role-based access to system resources.

### 4.2 Course Management

Provides facilities for creating, organizing, publishing, and managing
courses.

### 4.3 Learning Content Management

Allows learning materials to be organized into a structured hierarchy such
as courses, chapters, and lessons.

Learning content may include different forms of educational materials such
as documents, videos, and other supported resources.

### 4.4 Enrollment Management

Manages the relationship between students and the courses in which they
participate.

### 4.5 Learning Progress Tracking

Records and maintains information about a student's progress through course
content.

### 4.6 Assessment Management

Supports the creation and delivery of learning assessments and records
student assessment results.

### 4.7 Learning Interaction

Provides mechanisms that allow students and lecturers to communicate and
interact within the learning environment.

### 4.8 Notification

Provides system notifications related to relevant learning activities and
events.

### 4.9 Administration and Reporting

Provides administrative capabilities for managing the platform and viewing
general system and learning information.

### 4.10 Learning Analytics and Early Warning

Collects and analyzes learning-related information such as:

- learning progress;
- assessment performance;
- learning activity;
- inactivity;
- missed or late submissions;
- engagement indicators.

The analytics component uses these indicators to generate a risk assessment
for a student within a course.

A risk assessment may contain:

- a risk level;
- factors contributing to the assessment;
- supporting learning indicators.

The resulting information is presented to lecturers to support decisions
about appropriate interventions.

---

## 5. Core Domain Overview

The core domain of Smart Campus revolves around the following concepts:

### User

Represents a person who interacts with the platform under an authorized role.

### Course

Represents an organized learning offering managed by a lecturer and
participated in by students.

### Enrollment

Represents the participation of a student in a course.

### Enrollment Status History

Represents the recorded sequence of changes to a student's participation
status in a course.

### Chapter

Represents a major organizational section of a course.

### Lesson

Represents an individual learning unit contained within a chapter.

### Learning Progress

Represents the progress of a student through learning content.

### Assessment

Represents an activity used to evaluate student learning.

### Assessment Attempt

Represents a student's participation in an assessment and its resulting
outcome.

### Learning Activity

Represents relevant student activity recorded during interaction with the
learning platform.

### Risk Assessment

Represents the system's assessment of a student's learning risk within a
specific course.

### Risk Factor

Represents a factor contributing to a generated risk assessment.

### Intervention

Represents an action taken by a lecturer to support a student after reviewing
learning progress or risk information.

---

## 6. High-Level Learning Flow

A typical learning process is:

1. A lecturer creates and prepares a course.
2. Learning content is organized into chapters and lessons.
3. Students enroll in or are enrolled in the course.
4. Students access learning materials and participate in learning activities.
5. Students complete assessments during the course.
6. The system records learning progress, activities, and assessment results.
7. Lecturers monitor student and course progress.

---

## 7. Learning Analytics and Early Warning Flow

The Learning Analytics and Early Warning process operates alongside the
normal learning process.

A high-level flow is:

Student Learning Activities
        â†“
Learning Data Collection
        â†“
Learning Indicator Aggregation
        â†“
Risk Assessment
        â†“
Risk Level and Contributing Factors
        â†“
Lecturer Analytics Dashboard
        â†“
Lecturer Intervention

The analytics component is intended to assist lecturers rather than replace
their academic judgment.

---

## 8. System Boundaries

Smart Campus focuses on the management and monitoring of online learning
activities within a university learning environment.

The initial system does not aim to provide:

- live video-conferencing infrastructure;
- payment processing;
- native mobile applications;
- advanced AI tutoring;
- a replacement for lecturer academic decisions.

These capabilities may be considered as future extensions but are outside
the initial project scope.

---

## 9. High-Level System Architecture

Smart Campus follows a web-based client-server architecture.

The system consists of:

- a web frontend used by students, lecturers, and administrators;
- a backend application providing application and business services;
- a relational database for persistent application and learning data;
- storage for learning materials;
- a Learning Analytics component integrated with the learning platform.

The Learning Analytics component consumes learning and assessment data
generated by the core LMS and produces risk information that can be presented
to lecturers.

Detailed architectural and implementation decisions are documented
separately.

---

## 10. Requirement References

Detailed system requirements are maintained separately from this
specification.

They are divided into:

- Functional Requirements (FR)
- Non-Functional Requirements (NFR)

Functional Requirements define what behaviors and capabilities the system
must provide.

Non-Functional Requirements define quality attributes and operational
constraints such as security, performance, reliability, usability, and
maintainability.

# User Access Requirements

## 1. Overview
- Module Description: Manages user accounts, authentication, and role-based access for the Smart Campus web platform.
- Scope: Covers administrator-provisioned accounts, sign-in and sign-out, account status and role management, profile and credential updates, and authorization of protected resources. Course enrollment and lecturer-to-course assignments are managed by their respective modules; this module uses those relationships when checking access. External identity providers and public self-registration are outside the initial scope.
- Cross-module note: Deactivating an account does not alter the user's enrollments; see BR-ENROLL-007.

## 2. Actors
- Student: Signs in to participate in enrolled courses and manages their own account information.
- Lecturer: Signs in to manage assigned courses and view information about students in those courses.
- Administrator: Creates and manages accounts, roles, and account status across the platform.

## 3. Functional Requirements
### FR-ACCESS-001 - Create User Account
- Description: The system must allow an administrator to create a user account with a unique login identifier, initial credentials, and at least one authorized role: Student, Lecturer, or Administrator. Accounts are active by default, but the Administrator may create an account in inactive state.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ACCESS-002 - Authenticate User
- Description: The system must verify a user's login identifier and credentials, confirm that the account is active, and establish an authenticated session only when all checks succeed.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ACCESS-003 - Sign Out
- Description: The system must allow an authenticated user to sign out and invalidate the current session so it can no longer access protected resources.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ACCESS-004 - Enforce Role and Resource Permissions
- Description: The system must authorize each protected action using the user's role and relevant resource relationship. A Student may access their own permitted information and available content in courses with ACTIVE enrollment; a Lecturer may manage and inspect only assigned courses and their students; an Administrator may perform system-level management. The same checks must apply to direct requests as to navigation in the user interface.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ACCESS-005 - Manage Account Roles and Status
- Description: The system must allow an administrator to view accounts, update their assigned roles, and activate or deactivate accounts. Role or status changes must invalidate the affected account's existing sessions so outdated permissions cannot be used.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ACCESS-006 - Update Own Profile
- Description: The system must allow an authenticated user to view and update supported personal profile fields while preventing changes to their own roles, account status, or login identifier through profile editing.
- Priority: Should-have

### FR-ACCESS-007 - Change or Reset Credentials
- Description: The system must allow an authenticated user to change their own password after verifying the current password, and allow an Administrator to initiate a credential reset when the user cannot sign in. A reset must issue a single-use temporary credential to the account holder without disclosing a usable password to the Administrator; it must expire after a configured period and require a password change at the next successful sign-in before any protected resource is accessible. Existing sessions for that account must be invalidated after a successful password change or reset.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ACCESS-008 - Protect Learning and Analytics Data
- Description: The system must allow a Student to view their own progress, activity, and assessment results, but must deny the Student access to their own risk level, risk factors, and contributing indicators as presented in a risk assessment. The system must restrict a Lecturer to records and risk assessments for Students in assigned courses, and an Administrator to authorized system-level views.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ACCESS-009 - Limit Authentication Attempts
- Description: The system must rate-limit authentication attempts per account and per source, temporarily lock out attempts after a configured number of consecutive failures, and use the same generic failure response for invalid credentials and lockout.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ACCESS-010 - Record Administrative Actions
- Description: The system must append an administrative audit record for account creation, role change, account activation or deactivation, credential reset, enrollment override, and removal of a Student from a course. Each record must contain the acting user, target, action, timestamp, and reason where required. Audit records must be readable only by authorized Administrators and must never be modified or deleted.
- Priority: Must-have

## 4. Use Cases
### UC-ACCESS-001 - Create User Account
- Related Requirements: FR-ACCESS-001, FR-ACCESS-004, FR-ACCESS-010
- Primary Actor: Administrator
- Preconditions:
    * The administrator is authenticated and authorized to manage users.
- Trigger: The administrator chooses to create an account.
- Main Flow:
    1. The system displays the account creation form.
    2. The administrator enters a login identifier, initial credentials, required profile details, and role.
    3. The system validates the required information and checks identifier uniqueness.
    4. The system creates an active account by default, or an inactive account if selected, stores its assigned role, and appends the administrative audit record.
    5. The system confirms creation to the administrator.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Create Inactive Account: The administrator selects inactive status; the system stores the account but prevents sign-in until activation.
    * A2 - Cancel Creation: The administrator cancels; no account is created.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Duplicate Identifier: The system rejects the identifier and requests a unique one.
    * E2 - Invalid Data: The system identifies missing or invalid fields and requests correction.
    * E3 - Unauthorized Request: The system rejects account creation by a user without administrator permission.
- Postconditions:
    * A new account with its role and status is stored, or no account is created if the flow fails or is canceled.

### UC-ACCESS-002 - Sign In
- Related Requirements: FR-ACCESS-002, FR-ACCESS-004, FR-ACCESS-007, FR-ACCESS-009
- Primary Actor: Student, Lecturer, Administrator
- Preconditions:
    * The user has an existing account and is not authenticated in the current session.
- Trigger: The user submits a login identifier and password.
- Main Flow:
    1. The system receives the credentials.
    2. The system verifies the identifier and password.
    3. The system confirms that the account is active.
    4. The system establishes an authenticated session with the user's current roles.
    5. The system displays the authorized starting page.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Reset Credential Sign-In: After a reset under UC-ACCESS-007, the user presents the single-use temporary credential. The system permits only the required password-change flow; once the new password is set, it consumes the temporary credential and establishes an ordinary session. No protected resource is accessible before that change.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Invalid Credentials: The system denies sign-in and displays a generic failure message.
    * E2 - Inactive Account: The system denies sign-in using the generic failure message.
    * E3 - Expired Temporary Credential: The system denies sign-in using the generic failure message; a new reset under UC-ACCESS-007 is required.
    * E4 - Rate Limit or Temporary Lockout: The system denies the attempt using the same generic failure message as E1.
- Postconditions:
    * A session exists only after successful authentication; unsuccessful attempts grant no access.

### UC-ACCESS-003 - Sign Out
- Related Requirements: FR-ACCESS-003
- Primary Actor: Student, Lecturer, Administrator
- Preconditions:
    * The user has an active authenticated session.
- Trigger: The user selects Sign Out.
- Main Flow:
    1. The system invalidates the current session.
    2. The system returns the user to a public or sign-in page.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Already Expired Session: The system directs the user to sign in again.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Protected Request After Sign-Out: The system rejects the request and requires a new sign-in.
- Postconditions:
    * The previous session cannot be used to access protected resources.

### UC-ACCESS-004 - Manage User Role or Account Status
- Related Requirements: FR-ACCESS-004, FR-ACCESS-005, FR-ACCESS-010
- Primary Actor: Administrator
- Preconditions:
    * The administrator is authenticated and the target account exists.
- Trigger: The administrator selects a user account to update.
- Main Flow:
    1. The system displays the account's roles and status.
    2. The administrator changes the role assignment or account status.
    3. The system validates the requested change and administrator permission.
    4. The system saves the change, invalidates the affected account's existing sessions, and appends the administrative audit record.
    5. The system confirms the updated account details.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Cancel Change: The administrator leaves without saving; the account remains unchanged.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Invalid Role or Status: The system rejects the change and requests a valid selection.
    * E2 - Account No Longer Exists: The system reports that the account cannot be updated.
    * E3 - Unauthorized Request: The system rejects the update.
- Postconditions:
    * Successful changes are stored; previous sessions cannot continue using outdated permissions.

### UC-ACCESS-005 - Update Own Profile
- Related Requirements: FR-ACCESS-006
- Primary Actor: Student, Lecturer, Administrator
- Preconditions:
    * The user is authenticated and has an active account.
- Trigger: The user opens and edits their profile.
- Main Flow:
    1. The system displays the user's editable profile fields.
    2. The user changes supported fields and submits them.
    3. The system validates the submitted values.
    4. The system saves and displays the updated profile.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Cancel Edit: The user cancels; the existing profile is retained.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Invalid Profile Data: The system reports errors and keeps the prior values.
    * E2 - Restricted Field Change: The system rejects attempts to alter roles, status, or login identifier through this flow.
- Postconditions:
    * Only permitted profile fields are updated.

### UC-ACCESS-006 - Change Password
- Related Requirements: FR-ACCESS-007
- Primary Actor: Student, Lecturer, Administrator
- Preconditions:
    * The user is authenticated and has an active account.
- Trigger: The user chooses to change their password.
- Main Flow:
    1. The system requests the current and new passwords.
    2. The user submits both values.
    3. The system verifies the current password and validates the new one against the configured password policy.
    4. The system replaces the credentials and invalidates existing sessions for the account.
    5. The system asks the user to sign in with the new password.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Cancel Change: The user cancels and retains the current password.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Incorrect Current Password: The system rejects the change.
    * E2 - Invalid New Password: The system explains the applicable policy and requests another password.
- Postconditions:
    * The new password is required for subsequent authentication after a successful change.

### UC-ACCESS-007 - Reset User Credentials
- Related Requirements: FR-ACCESS-005, FR-ACCESS-007, FR-ACCESS-010
- Primary Actor: Administrator
- Preconditions:
    * The administrator is authenticated and the target account exists.
- Trigger: The administrator selects Reset Credentials for the account.
- Main Flow:
    1. The system verifies the administrator's permission and displays the target account.
    2. The administrator confirms the reset.
    3. The system issues a single-use temporary credential to the account holder without showing it to the Administrator, sets its configured expiry, requires a password change on its next successful use before granting protected access, and invalidates existing sessions.
    4. The system appends an administrative audit record and confirms the reset to the Administrator without disclosing the credential.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Cancel Reset: The administrator cancels; the account is unchanged.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Account Not Found: The system rejects the reset.
    * E2 - Unauthorized Request: The system rejects the reset.
- Postconditions:
    * The account holder must use the temporary credential and set a new password before protected access; no prior session remains valid. An expired temporary credential follows UC-ACCESS-002/E3.

### UC-ACCESS-008 - Access Protected Course or Learning Data
- Related Requirements: FR-ACCESS-004, FR-ACCESS-008
- Primary Actor: Student, Lecturer, Administrator
- Preconditions:
    * A protected resource exists and the user is authenticated with an active account.
- Trigger: The user opens or submits a request for a course resource, learning record, or risk assessment.
- Main Flow:
    1. The system identifies the requested resource and action.
    2. The system checks the user's role, the applicable enrollment or course assignment, and the course publication state and content availability where relevant.
    3. The system returns the resource or performs the action when all checks pass.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Administrator Access: The system applies administrator permissions to authorized system-level resources.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - No ACTIVE Enrollment: The system denies Student access to restricted course content when no enrollment exists or its status is WITHDRAWN or REMOVED.
    * E2 - Unassigned Lecturer: The system denies access to another lecturer's course or student records.
    * E3 - Expired Session or Inactive Account: The system requires sign-in or denies access.
    * E4 - Student Risk Data Request: The system denies a Student access to their own risk level, risk factors, or contributing indicators in a risk assessment.
- Postconditions:
    * Only an authorized request obtains the protected resource or changes its state.

### UC-ACCESS-009 - View and Search Accounts
- Related Requirements: FR-ACCESS-004, FR-ACCESS-005
- Primary Actor: Administrator
- Preconditions:
    * The Administrator is authenticated and authorized to manage user accounts.
- Trigger: The Administrator opens the account list or submits a search.
- Main Flow:
    1. The system verifies the Administrator's permission.
    2. The system lists accounts with their roles and account status.
    3. The Administrator enters a search term or selects supported filters.
    4. The system displays matching accounts for selection.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - No Matches: The system displays an empty result without changing any account.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Unauthorized Request: The system denies access to the account list and search results.
- Postconditions:
    * No account is changed; only an authorized Administrator can view the results.

## 5. Business Rules
### BR-ACCESS-001 - Unique Account Identity
- Description: Each account must have a unique login identifier. Only an administrator can create accounts or assign roles; a user cannot grant themselves additional permissions by editing their profile.

### BR-ACCESS-002 - Active Account and Session Requirement
- Description: Protected actions require a valid session for an active account. Sign-out, administrator changes to account roles or status, and credential changes or resets invalidate affected sessions. Account deactivation does not change enrollment status (BR-ENROLL-007).

### BR-ACCESS-003 - Role and Relationship Based Access
- Description: Role alone does not grant course-scoped access. Student access to restricted course content requires an ACTIVE enrollment, a published course publication state, and content availability; Lecturer management and student-data access require assignment to that course. Unauthorized direct requests must be rejected.

### BR-ACCESS-004 - Credential Protection
- Description: Passwords must be stored using a one-way password hash and never exposed in account views. The configured password policy must require at least 12 characters, reject known-breached and trivially common passwords, and avoid composition rules that force predictable substitutions. Authentication attempts must be rate-limited per account and per source, with temporary lockout after a configured number of consecutive failures. Invalid credentials, lockout, and expired temporary credentials must use a generic failure response that does not reveal account existence or lockout state.
- Dependency: Configuration and management of the password policy belong to Administration and Reporting (specification.md Â§4.9).

### BR-ACCESS-005 - Learning Data Privacy
- Description: A Student may view their own progress, activity, and assessment results, but not their own risk level, risk factors, or contributing indicators in a risk assessment. A Lecturer may view student progress and risk information only for assigned courses; authorized Administrators may access system-level views. This exclusion is a deliberate design decision: risk assessment is lecturer-facing decision support, and exposing a risk label to its Student could create a self-fulfilling effect. One Student's records must not be disclosed to another Student.

### BR-ACCESS-006 - Session Revocation
- Description: Session validity must be verifiable against server-side state on every protected request, through a server-side session store or a per-account token version compared on each request. Role changes, account deactivation, password changes, and credential resets must revoke affected sessions immediately rather than wait for token expiry.

# Course Content Requirements

## 1. Overview
- Module Description: Allows learning materials to be organized into a structured hierarchy such as courses, chapters and lessons. It also enables students to access learning content and interact with educational materials.
- Scope: Covers the creation, updating, and structuring of learning
content, supporting multiple formats including documents, videos,
and other supported resources. It also includes permission-based
access for students participating in a course. Live video-conferencing infrastructure
and learning progress tracking are outside the initial scope.

## 2. Actors
- Lecturer: Responsible for organizing course content, managing learning activities and delivering learning materials.
- Student: A learner participating in the course who accesses learning materials and interacts with learning content.

## 3. Functional Requirements

### FR-CONTENT-001 - Hierarchical Content Organization
- Description: The system must allow lecturers to organize educational materials into a structured hierarchy consisting of courses, chapters, and lessons.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-CONTENT-002 - Chapter Management
- Description: The system must allow lecturers to create, update and organize chapters as the major organizational sections of a course.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-CONTENT-003 - Lesson Management
- Description: The system must allow lecturers to create, update and manage individual learning lessons contained within a chapter.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-CONTENT-004 - Multi-Format Learning Materials Support
- Description: The system must support the storage and attachment of various educational resources to lessons, including documents, videos, and other supported educational formats.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-CONTENT-005 - Student Learning Content Access
- Description: The system must allow enrolled students to access, view and interact with learning content and materials published in their courses.
- Priority: Must-have

## 4. Use Cases

### UC-CONTENT-001 - Create Chapter
- Related Requirements: FR-CONTENT-001, FR-CONTENT-002
- Primary Actor: Lecturer
- Preconditions:
    * The lecturer is authenticated.
    * The lecturer is assigned to manage the target course.
    * The target course exists.
- Trigger: The lecturer chooses to create a new chapter.
- Main Flow:
    1. The lecturer navigates to the course content management interface.
    2. The lecturer selects the option to create a new chapter.
    3. The system displays a new chapter creation form.
    4. The lecturer enters the chapter title and optional metadata.
    5. The lecturer submits the chapter details.
    6. The system validates the submitted information.
    7. The system creates the chapter and associates it with the selected course.
    8. The system saves the chapter in the database.
    9. The system displays the newly created chapter in the course hierarchy.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Cancel Creation: The lecturer cancels the creation process. The system discards unsaved information and returns to the course content interface.
    * A2 - Specify Initial Position: The lecturer selects an initial position for the chapter. The system stores the chapter at the specified position.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Missing Chapter Title: The system displays a validation error and requests a valid title.
    * E2 - Unauthorized Access: The system rejects the operation if the lecturer does not have permission to manage the course.
- Postconditions:
    * A new chapter is stored in the database.
    * The chapter is associated with the target course.
    * The course hierarchy displays the new chapter.

### UC-CONTENT-002 - Update Chapter
- Related Requirements: FR-CONTENT-002
- Primary Actor: Lecturer
- Preconditions:
    * The lecturer is authenticated.
    * The lecturer has permission to manage the target course.
    * The target chapter exists.
- Trigger: The lecturer chooses to edit an existing chapter.
- Main Flow:
    1. The lecturer navigates to the course content management interface.
    2. The lecturer selects an existing chapter.
    3. The lecturer selects the edit chapter option.
    4. The system retrieves and displays the current chapter details.
    5. The lecturer modifies the chapter title or supported metadata.
    6. The lecturer submits the updated information.
    7. The system validates the updated details.
    8. The system updates the chapter in the database.
    9. The system displays the updated chapter information.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Cancel Update: The lecturer cancels the editing process. The system retains the original chapter details.
    * A2 - No changes: The lecturer submits without modifying any information. The system retains the existing details.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Invalid Chapter Details: The system displays a validation error and requests correction.
    * E2 - Chapter Not Found: The system informs the lecturer that the selected chapter does not exist.
    * E3 - Unauthorized Access: The system rejects the update operation if the lecturer lacks permission.
- Postconditions:
    * The chapter details are updated in the database.
    * The updated information is displayed in the course hierarchy.

### UC-CONTENT-003 - Organize Chapters
- Related Requirements: FR-CONTENT-001, FR-CONTENT-002
-  Primary Actor: Lecturer
- Preconditions:
    * The lecturer is authenticated.
    * The lecturer has permission to manage the target course.
    * The target course contains existing chapters.
- Trigger: The lecturer chooses to rearrange chapters within the course hierarchy.
- Main Flow:
    1. The lecturer navigates to the course content management interface.
    2. The system displays the existing chapters in their current order.
    3. The lecturer selects a chapter to rearrange.
    4. The lecturer changes the chapter's position in the hierarchy.
    5. The system validates the requested arrangement.
    6. The system updates the chapter ordering.
    7. The system saves the updated structure in the database.
    8. The system displays the revised chapter hierarchy.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Move Chapter Up: The lecturer moves a chapter to an earlier position.
    * A2 - Move Chapter Down: The lecturer moves a chapter to a later position.
    * A3 - Cancel Reordering: The lecturer cancels the arrangement before saving. The system retains the previous ordering.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Invalid Chapter Position: The system rejects an invalid ordering request.
    * E2 - Concurrent Modification: Another update has changed the chapter structure. The system informs the lecturer and requests a refresh or retry.
- Postconditions:
    * The chapter ordering is updated and stored in the database.
    * The course hierarchy reflects the new chapter sequence.

### UC-CONTENT-004 - Create Lesson
- Related Requirements: FR-CONTENT-001, FR-CONTENT-003

- Preconditions:
    * The lecturer is authenticated.

    4. The system displays the lesson creation form.
    5. The lecturer enters the lesson title and learning unit details.
    6. The lecturer submits the lesson information.
    7. The system validates the submitted details.
    8. The system creates the lesson and associates it with the selected chapter.
    9. The system saves the lesson in the database.
    10. The system displays the newly created lesson within the chapter.
- Alternative Flows: 
    * A1 - Cancel Creation: The lecturer cancels the creation process. The system discards unsaved information.
    * A2 - Specify Lesson Position: The lecturer selects an initial position for the lesson. The system stores the lesson at the specified position.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Missing Lesson Title: The system displays an error and requests a valid title.
    * E2 - Invalid Chapter: The system rejects the request if the target chapter does not exist.
    * E3 - Unauthorized Access: The system rejects the operation if the lecturer lacks permission.
- Postconditions:
    * A new lesson is stored in the database.
    * The lesson is associated with the selected chapter.
    * The lesson is displayed in the chapter hierarchy.

### UC-CONTENT-005 - Update Lesson
- Related Requirements: FR-CONTENT-003
- Primary Actor: Lecturer
- Preconditions:
    * The lecturer is authenticated.
    * The lecturer has permission to manage the target course.
    * The target lesson exists.
- Trigger: The lecturer chooses to edit an existing lesson.
- Main Flow:
    1. The lecturer navigates to the course content management interface.
    2. The lecturer selects a chapter and an existing lesson.
    3. The lecturer chooses the edit lesson option.
    4. The system retrieves and displays the current lesson details.
    5. The lecturer modifies the lesson title or supported learning content.
    6. The lecturer submits the updated information.
    7. The system validates the updated details. 
    8. The system updates the lesson in the database.
    9. The system displays the updated lesson information.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Cancel Update: The lecturer cancels the editing process. The system retains the original lesson information.
    * A2 - Change Lesson Position: The lecturer changes the lesson's position within the chapter, if reordering is supported.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Invalid Lesson Details: The system displays a validation error.
    * E2 - Lesson Not Found: The system informs the lecturer that the selected lesson does not exist.
    * E3 - Unauthorized Access: The system rejects the update operation if the lecturer lacks permission.
- Postconditions:
    * The lesson details are updated in the database.
    * The updated lesson information is displayed within the chapter.

### UC-CONTENT-006 - Manage Learning Materials
- Related Requirements: FR-CONTENT-003, FR-CONTENT-004
- Primary Actor: Lecturer
- Preconditions:
    * The lecturer is authenticated.
    * The lecturer has permission to manage the target course.
    * The lecturer has access to the material management interface.
    * The target lesson exists.
- Trigger: The lecturer chooses to manage educational materials for a lesson.
- Main Flow:
    1. The lecturer navigates to the target lesson.
    2. The lecturer selects the option to manage learning materials.
    3. The lecturer chooses to upload or attach a new educational resource.
    4. The lecturer selects a supported document, video, or other educational format.
    5. The system validates the material format and relevant constraints.
    6. The system stores the material or its reference.
    7. The system associates the material with the selected lesson.
    8. The system displays the updated list of learning materials.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Update Material: The lecturer replaces a material or updates its metadata.
    * A2 - Remove Material: The lecturer selects an existing material for removal. The system asks for confirmation and removes its lesson association.
    * A3 - Attach External Video: The lecturer provides a supported external video reference. The system validates and stores the reference.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Unsupported File Format: The system rejects an unsupported file and displays an error message.
    * E2 - File Size Exceeded: The system rejects a file that exceeds the configured size limit.
    * E3 - Upload Failure: The system informs the lecturer that the upload failed and allows retrying.
    * E4 - Invalid External Reference: The system rejects an invalid or unsupported external video link.
- Postconditions:
    * The selected learning materials are associated with the lesson.
    * Material updates are stored in the database or supported storage system.
    * The updated material list is displayed.

### UC-CONTENT-007 - Browse Course Content
- Related Requirements: FR-CONTENT-001, FR-CONTENT-005
- Primary Actor: Student
- Preconditions:
    * The student is authenticated.
    * The student is enrolled in the target course.
    * The course is available to the student.
- Trigger: The student selects an enrolled course to access its learning content.
- Main Flow:
    1. The student navigates to the enrolled course.
    2. The system verifies the student's enrollment and access permissions.
    3. The system retrieves the course hierarchy.
    4. The system displays the course's chapters and lessons.
    5. The student selects a chapter to expand or view its lessons.
    6. The system displays the lessons belonging to the selected chapter.
    7. The student selects a lesson to access its content.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Expand or Collapse Chapter: The student expands or collapses a chapter to navigate the course structure.
    * A2 - Navigate Between Chapters: The student selects a different chapter from the course hierarchy.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Access Denied: The system denies access if the student is not enrolled or does not have the required permissions.
    * E2 - Course Not Available: The system informs the student that the course is not currently accessible.
- Postconditions:
    * The student can view the available course hierarchy.
    * The student can select a lesson for further content access.

### UC-CONTENT-008 - View and Interact with Learning Content
- Related Requirements: FR-CONTENT-004, FR-CONTENT-005
- Primary Actor: Student
- Preconditions:
    * The student is authenticated.
    * The student is enrolled in the target course.
    * The target lesson exists and is available.
    * The lesson contains published learning content or materials.
- Trigger: The student selects a lesson to study.
- Main Flow:
    1. The student selects a lesson from the course hierarchy.
    2. The system verifies the student's access permissions.
    3. The system retrieves the lesson details and associated learning materials.
    4. The system displays the lesson content.
    5. The student views the lesson content.
    6. The student opens or plays supported educational materials.
    7. The system provides the relevant content interaction features.
    8. The student finishes viewing or interacting with the lesson.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - View Document: The student opens a supported document. The system displays or provides access to the document.
    * A2 - Play Video: The student selects a video. The system provides the video player or supported video reference.
    * A3 - Open External Material: The student selects an external learning resource. The system provides the supported resource link.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Access Denied: The system denies access if the student is not authorized to view the lesson.
    * E2 - Material Unavailable: The system informs the student when an associated learning material cannot be retrieved.
    * E3 - Unsupported Content: The system informs the student when a material cannot be displayed using the supported access method.
- Postconditions: 
    * The student has accessed the lesson content.
    * The student has been provided with the available supported learning materials.

## 5. Business Rules

### BR-CONTENT-001 - Hierarchical Content Structure
- Description: Each lesson must belong to one chapter, and each chapter must belong to one course. The system must maintain the hierarchy of Course â†’ Chapter â†’ Lesson. A lesson cannot exist without an associated chapter, and a chapter cannot exist without an associated course.

### BR-CONTENT-002 - Content Management Authorization
- Description: Only lecturers assigned to a course and authorized to manage that course may create, update, organize, or remove its chapters, lessons, learning materials. Students may access published course content but may not modify the course structure or learning materials.

### BR-CONTENT-003 - Chapter and Lesson Ordering
- Description: Chapters within a course and lessons within a chapter must have an identifiable order. The system must preserve the configured order when displaying course content to students. Reordering content must not change the association between a chapter and its course or between a lesson and its chapter.

### BR-CONTENT-004 - Supported Learning Material Formats
- Description: The system may only accept learning materials in supported formats and within the configured file size limits. Each learning material must be associated with at least one lesson. Unsupported file formats or invalid external material references must be rejected.

### BR-CONTENT-005 - Course Content Access
- Description: Only authenticated students enrolled in and authorized to access a course may view its available learning content. Students may access only content that has been published or made available to them. Users without the required permissions must not be allowed to access restricted course content.

### BR-CONTENT-006 - Content Availability and Updates
- Description: Learning content must be available to students only when it satisfies the configured publication and access conditions. Updating or removing learning materials must not grant unauthorized access to the affected content. The system must clearly indicate when a learning material is unavailable or has been removed.

# Enrollment Requirements

## 1. Overview
- Module Description: Manages the relationship between Students and the courses in which they participate.
- Scope: Covers student self-enrollment, enrollment by an authorized Lecturer or Administrator, course rosters, a Student's enrolled-course list, and withdrawal or removal from a course. Course creation and publication belong to Course Management; lesson access belongs to Course Content; progress, assessments, and risk calculations belong to their respective modules. Enrollment supplies their course-participation context.
- Dependency: Course Management owns three distinct attributes used here: course publication state, the enrollment window (whether the course accepts new enrollments), and content availability. Course Content applies content availability when serving published materials. Enrollment decisions use course publication state and the enrollment window; an enrollment alone does not make content available.

## 2. Actors
- Student: Enrolls in available courses, views their course participation, and withdraws when allowed.
- Lecturer: Views and manages enrollment in courses to which they are assigned.
- Administrator: Manages enrollment and course participation across the platform.

## 3. Functional Requirements
### FR-ENROLL-001 - Enroll in Available Course
- Description: The system must allow an authenticated Student to enroll when the course publication state is published and the enrollment window accepts new enrollments. Successful enrollment must create or reactivate an ACTIVE Student-Course relationship.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ENROLL-002 - Enroll Student by Authorized Staff
- Description: The system must allow an assigned Lecturer or an Administrator to enroll an existing, active Student when the enrollment window accepts new enrollments. The system must allow only an Administrator to override a closed enrollment window through an explicit, separately confirmed action with a mandatory reason; the override must record the acting Administrator, timestamp, and reason in Enrollment Status History and the administrative audit log. The override must only create or reactivate enrollment and must not change course publication state, content availability, or their access rules.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ENROLL-003 - Prevent Duplicate Active Enrollment
- Description: The system must enforce at most one Enrollment record per (Student, Course) pair with a uniqueness constraint at the persistence layer. Re-enrollment must reactivate that record through a conditional update, never through check-then-insert; concurrent requests must yield exactly one ACTIVE enrollment and treat losing requests as already enrolled.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ENROLL-004 - View Course Roster
- Description: The system must allow the assigned Lecturer and authorized Administrator to view a roster that defaults to ACTIVE enrollments and offers an explicit option to include WITHDRAWN and REMOVED entries. Each entry must show enrollment status, latest status-change date, and the Student's account status as a derived indicator.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ENROLL-005 - View My Courses
- Description: The system must allow a Student to view courses with ACTIVE enrollment and open course content only when the course publication state is published and content availability permits access.
- Dependency: Learning Progress owns grouping courses as in progress or completed and displaying progress percentages.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ENROLL-006 - Withdraw or Remove Enrollment
- Description: The system must allow a Student to change their own enrollment from ACTIVE to WITHDRAWN when course policy permits, and allow an assigned Lecturer or Administrator to change an authorized course enrollment from ACTIVE to REMOVED. The enrollment must cease to grant course access immediately after either transition.
- Priority: Should-have

### FR-ENROLL-007 - Maintain Enrollment Status and History
- Description: The system must keep Student, Course, current status, initial enrollment date, and latest status-change date on the Enrollment record. On initial creation and every status transition, the system must append an Enrollment Status History entry with the enrollment reference, previous status, new status, change timestamp, acting user, and optional reason. History entries must remain append-only through withdrawal, removal, and re-enrollment so Learning Analytics can derive periods of non-participation from transition history rather than current status alone; prior learning and assessment data must remain available for authorized historical reporting.
- Priority: Must-have

### 3.1 Enrollment Status Model

An Enrollment has exactly three statuses: `ACTIVE` (current participation), `WITHDRAWN` (the Student ended participation), and `REMOVED` (an authorized Lecturer or Administrator ended participation). Completion belongs to Learning Progress and never changes the Enrollment status. The terms "inactive enrollment" and "previous inactive enrollment" mean `WITHDRAWN` or `REMOVED`.

| From | To | Permitted Actor | Condition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ACTIVE | WITHDRAWN | Student (own enrollment) | Course policy permits withdrawal |
| ACTIVE | REMOVED | Assigned Lecturer, Administrator | Actor authorized for the course |
| WITHDRAWN | ACTIVE | Student, Assigned Lecturer, Administrator | Course permits enrollment |
| REMOVED | ACTIVE | Assigned Lecturer, Administrator only | Reinstatement decision |

No other transition is valid. A newly created Enrollment starts as `ACTIVE`; its first history entry has an empty previous-status field, which is not another status. For `WITHDRAWN` to `ACTIVE`, the audited Administrator override in UC-ENROLL-002/A3 is the sole exception to the enrollment-window condition above, not a new transition.

## 4. Use Cases
### UC-ENROLL-001 - Student Enrolls in a Course
- Related Requirements: FR-ENROLL-001, FR-ENROLL-003, FR-ENROLL-007
- Primary Actor: Student
- Preconditions:
    * The Student is authenticated with an active account.
    * The target course exists, its course publication state is published, and its enrollment window accepts new enrollments.
- Trigger: The Student selects Enroll on the course page.
- Main Flow:
    1. The system identifies the Student and target course.
    2. The system checks the course publication state, enrollment window, and whether an ACTIVE enrollment already exists.
    3. The Student confirms enrollment.
    4. The system creates an ACTIVE Enrollment or conditionally changes the existing WITHDRAWN Enrollment to ACTIVE, then appends the status history entry.
    5. The system confirms enrollment and adds the course to the Student's enrolled-course list.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Previously WITHDRAWN: The system reactivates the existing record when the enrollment window accepts new enrollments.
    * A2 - Cancel Enrollment: The Student cancels before confirmation; no enrollment changes.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Enrollment Window Closed or Course Unpublished: The system rejects the request and identifies the applicable enrollment restriction.
    * E2 - Already Enrolled: The system retains the existing ACTIVE enrollment and informs the Student, including when another concurrent request succeeded first.
    * E3 - Account Inactive: The system denies the request.
    * E4 - Previously REMOVED: The system denies self-enrollment until an authorized Lecturer or Administrator reinstates the Student.
- Postconditions:
    * On success, exactly one ACTIVE Enrollment exists for the Student and Course. Course content access still depends on content availability.

### UC-ENROLL-002 - Lecturer or Administrator Enrolls a Student
- Related Requirements: FR-ENROLL-002, FR-ENROLL-003, FR-ENROLL-007, FR-ACCESS-010
- Primary Actor: Lecturer, Administrator
- Preconditions:
    * The actor is authenticated and authorized to manage the target course.
    * The Student has an existing active account; the enrollment window accepts new enrollments for the normal flow.
- Trigger: The actor selects Add Student from the course roster.
- Main Flow:
    1. The system displays the target course roster and enrollment action.
    2. The actor selects an existing Student.
    3. The system verifies the Student's account, the enrollment window, the actor's permission, and absence of an ACTIVE enrollment.
    4. The system creates an ACTIVE Enrollment or conditionally changes an existing WITHDRAWN or REMOVED Enrollment to ACTIVE, then appends the status history entry.
    5. The system confirms the change and updates the roster.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Cancel: The actor cancels before saving; the roster is unchanged.
    * A2 - Previous WITHDRAWN or REMOVED Enrollment: The system reactivates the existing record when the actor is permitted by the status transition model.
    * A3 - Administrator Override: If the enrollment window is closed, only an Administrator may choose a separately confirmed override, enter a mandatory reason, and enroll or reinstate the Student. The system records the acting Administrator, timestamp, and reason in Enrollment Status History and the administrative audit log. The enrollment does not bypass course publication state or content availability.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Student Account Not Found or Inactive: The system rejects the enrollment.
    * E2 - Already Enrolled: The system does not create a duplicate, including when a concurrent request succeeded first.
    * E3 - Enrollment Window Closed: The system rejects the action unless the Administrator completes A3.
    * E4 - Lecturer Not Assigned: The system rejects the action.
    * E5 - Override Reason Missing: The system rejects the override without a reason.
- Postconditions:
    * On success, one ACTIVE Enrollment links the selected Student and Course; any override has both history and audit entries.

### UC-ENROLL-003 - View Course Roster
- Related Requirements: FR-ENROLL-004, FR-ENROLL-007
- Primary Actor: Lecturer, Administrator
- Preconditions:
    * The actor is authenticated and authorized to view the target course.
- Trigger: The actor opens the course roster.
- Main Flow:
    1. The system verifies the actor's permission for the course.
    2. The system retrieves the course's ACTIVE enrollments.
    3. The system displays the Students, enrollment status, latest status-change date, and derived account status.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Empty Roster: The system displays an empty state when there are no ACTIVE enrollments.
    * A2 - Include Participation History: The actor selects the history view; the system includes WITHDRAWN and REMOVED entries with their enrollment status, latest status-change date, and derived account status.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Course Not Found: The system reports that the course does not exist.
    * E2 - Unauthorized Access: The system denies the roster request.
- Postconditions:
    * The roster is displayed without changing enrollment data.

### UC-ENROLL-004 - Student Views Enrolled Courses
- Related Requirements: FR-ENROLL-005
- Primary Actor: Student
- Preconditions:
    * The Student is authenticated with an active account.
- Trigger: The Student opens My Courses.
- Main Flow:
    1. The system retrieves the Student's ACTIVE enrollments.
    2. The system shows the associated courses, course publication state, and content availability.
    3. The Student selects a published course with available content to open its published materials.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Progress View: Learning Progress groups the courses as in progress or completed, orders them by recent access, and displays any available progress percentage.
    * A2 - No Enrollments: The system displays an empty state and offers navigation to courses whose course publication state is published.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Content Unavailable: The system shows the ACTIVE enrollment but does not open restricted course content when content availability prevents access.
    * E2 - Enrollment WITHDRAWN or REMOVED: The system excludes the course from the ACTIVE list and denies enrollment-based access to its content.
    * E3 - Course Unpublished: The system shows the ACTIVE enrollment but does not open restricted course content when course publication state is unpublished.
- Postconditions:
    * No enrollment data changes; only courses with ACTIVE enrollment are shown as current participation.

### UC-ENROLL-005 - Student Withdraws from a Course
- Related Requirements: FR-ENROLL-006, FR-ENROLL-007
- Primary Actor: Student
- Preconditions:
    * The Student is authenticated and has an ACTIVE enrollment in the course.
    * The course permits student withdrawal.
- Trigger: The Student selects Withdraw from the enrolled course.
- Main Flow:
    1. The system displays the target enrollment and requests confirmation.
    2. The Student confirms withdrawal.
    3. The system changes the enrollment status from ACTIVE to WITHDRAWN, updates the latest status-change date, and appends a status history entry.
    4. The system removes the course from the Student's ACTIVE enrolled-course list and revokes access to restricted course content.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Cancel: The Student cancels; enrollment remains ACTIVE.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Withdrawal Not Permitted: The system rejects the request and retains the ACTIVE enrollment.
    * E2 - No ACTIVE Enrollment: The system reports that there is no ACTIVE enrollment to withdraw.
- Postconditions:
    * The participation record remains for history, but it no longer grants course access.

### UC-ENROLL-006 - Lecturer or Administrator Removes a Student
- Related Requirements: FR-ENROLL-006, FR-ENROLL-007, FR-ACCESS-010
- Primary Actor: Lecturer, Administrator
- Preconditions:
    * The actor is authenticated and authorized to manage the course.
    * The selected Student has an ACTIVE enrollment in that course.
- Trigger: The actor selects Remove Student on the roster.
- Main Flow:
    1. The system displays the target Student and enrollment for confirmation.
    2. The actor confirms removal.
    3. The system changes the enrollment status from ACTIVE to REMOVED, updates the latest status-change date, and appends a status history entry and an administrative audit entry.
    4. The system updates the roster and revokes the Student's access to restricted course content.
- Alternative Flows:
    * A1 - Cancel: The actor cancels; enrollment remains ACTIVE.
- Exception Flows:
    * E1 - Lecturer Not Assigned: The system denies the removal.
    * E2 - No ACTIVE Enrollment: The system reports that the Student is not currently enrolled.
- Postconditions:
    * The Student no longer appears on the active roster; historical participation and learning data are retained.

## 5. Business Rules
### BR-ENROLL-001 - One Active Enrollment Per Student and Course
- Description: A persistence-layer uniqueness constraint must permit at most one Enrollment record per (Student, Course) pair, regardless of status. Re-enrollment must conditionally update that record to ACTIVE rather than use check-then-insert. Concurrent requests must resolve to exactly one ACTIVE enrollment; losing requests follow the already-enrolled exception flow.

### BR-ENROLL-002 - Enrollment Eligibility
- Description: Self-enrollment requires an active Student account, a course publication state set to published, and an enrollment window accepting new enrollments. Normal staff enrollment requires an active Student account, an enrollment window accepting new enrollments, and an authorized Administrator or assigned Lecturer. Only an Administrator may override a closed enrollment window through a separately confirmed action with a mandatory reason recorded with the acting Administrator and timestamp in Enrollment Status History and the administrative audit log. The override creates or reactivates enrollment only; it does not change course publication state, content availability, or their access rules.

### BR-ENROLL-003 - Enrollment-Based Content Access
- Description: An ACTIVE enrollment is required for enrollment-based access to course content. Course publication state determines whether the course is published. The enrollment window determines whether new enrollment is accepted, without itself changing an existing Student's content access. Content availability independently determines whether published materials can be opened. A transition to WITHDRAWN or REMOVED revokes enrollment-based access immediately.

### BR-ENROLL-004 - Course-Scoped Management
- Description: A Lecturer may view or change enrollments only in assigned courses. An authorized Administrator may manage enrollments across courses. A Student may view or withdraw only their own enrollment.

### BR-ENROLL-005 - Participation and Learning History
- Description: The Enrollment record holds Student, Course, current status, initial enrollment date, and latest status-change date as fast-path fields. Initial creation and every transition append an Enrollment Status History entry containing the enrollment reference, previous status, new status, change timestamp, acting user, and optional reason; previous status is empty only for initial creation. These entries are append-only and are never modified or deleted by withdrawal, removal, or re-enrollment. Learning Analytics must derive periods of non-participation from this history rather than current status alone. Existing progress and assessment results remain available for authorized historical reporting. Course completion belongs to Learning Progress and does not change Enrollment status.

### BR-ENROLL-006 - Re-enrollment
- Description: A WITHDRAWN Enrollment may return to ACTIVE while the enrollment window accepts new enrollments, except for an audited Administrator override under UC-ENROLL-002/A3. A REMOVED Enrollment may return to ACTIVE only by a reinstatement decision from an assigned Lecturer or Administrator; a closed enrollment window additionally requires the Administrator override. Reactivation must reuse the single Enrollment record and preserve its status history and existing learning history.

### BR-ENROLL-007 - Account Status and Enrollment Independence
- Description: Deactivating a user account must not change any enrollment status; account lifecycle is system-scoped while enrollment lifecycle is course-scoped. BR-ACCESS-002 already denies access for inactive accounts without an enrollment transition. The roster must display the Student's account status as a derived indicator alongside enrollment status so an assigned Lecturer can identify an ACTIVE enrollee who cannot sign in. Learning Analytics must exclude periods of account deactivation when computing inactivity and engagement indicators to avoid a false at-risk signal.
