# Learning Progress Requirements

## 1. Overview
- This module tracks a student's learning progress within a course: marking lessons as complete, saving the last accessed position, and displaying a progress bar.
- It is also the most important source of behavioral data (`LearningActivity`) for the Learning Analytics module (07) â€” relevant learning events must be logged with enough detail for module 07 to compute a risk score.

## 2. Actors
- Student
- Lecturer (view-only, cannot edit)

## 3. Functional Requirements
### FR-PROG-001 - Mark Lesson as Complete
- Description: The system automatically marks a lesson as complete once it reaches a threshold percentage based on content type: video (furthest second watched / total duration), PDF/slide (furthest page reached / total pages), quiz (submitted at least once). Plain-text content, which has no "page/second" measure, uses a manual "Mark as done" button.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-PROG-002 - Save and Resume Last Position
- Description: The system saves the last lesson/position the student accessed in the course and allows them to resume exactly at that position on their next visit.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-PROG-003 - Display Course Progress
- Description: The system calculates and displays the progress percentage (progress bar) for each enrolled course, based on the number of completed lessons out of the total required lessons.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-PROG-004 - List In-Progress and Completed Courses
- Description: The "My Courses" page displays a list of in-progress and completed (100%) courses, sorted by most recent access.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-PROG-005 - Record Learning Activity Events
- Description: The system records discrete learning activity events (login, viewing a lesson, completing a lesson, video/PDF viewing progress, submission time) into the `LearningActivity` store for consumption by the Learning Analytics module. Video and PDF share the same event schema, differing only in the unit of measurement:

The `current` value is always the **furthest position reached** (max second / max page), not the current position at the time the event is sent â€” this prevents students from rewinding a video or flipping back pages from skewing the actual completion percentage.
- Priority: Must-have (prerequisite for module 07)

### FR-PROG-006 - Lecturer Views Student Progress
- Description: The lecturer can view aggregated progress for the whole class as well as detailed per-lesson progress for each student.
- Priority: Should-have

## 4. Use Cases
### UC-PROG-001 - Resume Learning from Last Position
- Related Requirements: FR-PROG-001, FR-PROG-002
- Primary Actor: Student
- Preconditions: The student is enrolled in the course and has previously accessed at least one lesson.
- Trigger: The student opens an enrolled course.
- Main Flow: 1. The student opens the course.
2. The system retrieves the last accessed position.
3. The system takes the student back to that exact position ("Continue Learning").
4. The student continues learning; when the completion threshold is reached, the system marks the lesson as complete and records a `LearningActivity` event.
- Alternative Flows: The student chooses to study a different lesson instead of resuming.
- Exception Flows: No prior progress exists â†’ open the course's first lesson.
- Postconditions: `LearningProgress` is updated; a `LearningActivity` event is recorded.

### UC-PROG-002 - View My Progress Dashboard
- Related Requirements: FR-PROG-003, FR-PROG-004
- Primary Actor: Student
- Preconditions: The user is logged in.
- Trigger: The user visits the "My Courses" page.
- Main Flow: 1. The system retrieves all courses the student is enrolled in.
2. The system calculates the completion percentage for each course.
3. The system displays them grouped as In Progress / Completed, each with a progress bar.
- Exception Flows: No courses enrolled â†’ display an empty state suggesting the course catalogue.
- Postconditions: None (read-only).

## 5. Business Rules
### BR-PROG-001 - Completion Criteria by Content Type
- Description: A common formula applies to content with continuously measurable progress: `completedPercent = value.current / value.total` (video: seconds; PDF: pages). A lesson is considered complete when `completedPercent` â‰¥ 90%. Quizzes require at least one submission. Plain-text content (no pages/duration) uses the manual "Mark as done" button.

### BR-PROG-002 - Progress Percentage Formula
- Description: Course progress % = (number of completed lessons / total required lessons) Ã— 100. Optional/non-required lessons are not counted in the denominator.

### BR-PROG-003 - Resume Granularity
- Description: For video, the resume position is stored at the second level (`value.current`); for PDF, at the page level (`value.current`); for all other content types (plain text), resume is at the lesson level.

### BR-PROG-004 - Activity Logging Throttling
- Description: High-frequency events (e.g., video progress) are throttled to at most one write every 15â€“30 seconds.

# Assessment Requirements

## 1. Overview
- Module Description: Manages assessment-related activities in the Smart Campus platform, including question banks, assessment configuration, online assessment attempts, automatic grading for objective questions, manual grading for essay questions, and release of assessment results and feedback.
- Scope: Covers question management, assessment creation and publication, assessment attempts, grading, scores, attempt history, feedback, and assessment-level performance information. Course and content management belong to their respective modules. Enrollment determines whether a Student participates in a course. Learning Analytics owns risk-indicator extraction, weighted-sum risk-score calculation, risk classification, risk factors, and early-warning functionality.
- Cross-module note: Assessment results and attempt data are made available to Learning Analytics as input data. This module does not calculate or expose academic risk scores or risk levels.

## 2. Actors
- Student: Takes available assessments and views released scores, attempt history, answer details, and Lecturer feedback when permitted.
- Lecturer: Manages question banks and assessments for assigned courses, reviews submissions, manually grades essay responses, releases results, and views assessment-level performance information.
- Administrator: Performs authorized system-level administration and oversight. Assessment actions remain subject to the same course- and role-based authorization rules defined by User Access.

## 3. Functional Requirements
### FR-ASSESSMENT-001 - Manage Question Bank

- Description: The system must allow an authorized Lecturer to create, view, update, delete, search, and categorize questions for assigned courses. Supported question types must include multiple-choice, true/false, and essay questions. Questions may be categorized by topic and difficulty.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ASSESSMENT-002 - Create and Configure Assessment

- Description: The system must allow an authorized Lecturer to create and configure an assessment for an assigned course, including title, description, start and end times, duration, maximum attempts, optional access password, grading method, question selection, and question/option shuffling.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ASSESSMENT-003 - Manage Assessment Publication

- Description: The system must allow an authorized Lecturer to save an assessment as Draft, publish it for eligible Students, and update its configuration subject to assessment-state and attempt-history constraints.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ASSESSMENT-004 - Take Assessment

- Description: The system must allow an eligible Student with an ACTIVE enrollment to start and complete an available assessment within its configured time and attempt limits. The system must periodically save responses and automatically submit the current responses when the time limit expires.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ASSESSMENT-005 - Record Assessment Attempt

- Description: The system must record each assessment attempt with the Student, assessment, attempt number, start time, submission time, responses, attempt status, and resulting score information. Submitted attempt data must remain available for authorized historical reporting and Learning Analytics.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ASSESSMENT-006 - Automatically Grade Objective Questions

- Description: The system must automatically grade submitted multiple-choice and true/false responses using their configured answer keys and point values.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ASSESSMENT-007 - Manually Grade Essay Questions

- Description: The system must allow an authorized Lecturer to review submitted essay responses, assign scores within the configured point limits, add feedback, save grading progress, and finalize the assessment result.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ASSESSMENT-008 - View Assessment Results and Feedback

- Description: The system must allow a Student to view released results for their own assessment attempts, including final score, attempt history, answer details, and Lecturer feedback according to the configured result-release policy. Risk scores, risk levels, risk factors, and contributing risk indicators must not be exposed through assessment results.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ASSESSMENT-009 - View Assessment Performance

- Description: The system should allow an authorized Lecturer to view assessment-level performance information for an assigned course, such as number of submissions, completion rate, and score statistics. Authorized Administrators may access permitted system-level assessment information.
- Priority: Should-have

## 4. Use Cases
### UC-ASSESSMENT-001 - Manage Question Bank

- Related Requirements: FR-ASSESSMENT-001
- Primary Actor: Lecturer
- Preconditions: -   The Lecturer is authenticated and assigned to the target course.
- Trigger: The Lecturer opens the question bank for an assigned course.
- Main Flow: 1.  The system verifies the Lecturer's permission for the course.
    2.  The system displays the course question bank.
    3.  The Lecturer chooses to create or edit a question.
    4.  The Lecturer enters the question content, question type, answer information, point value, topic, and difficulty where applicable.
    5.  The system validates the submitted question data.
    6.  The system saves the question and displays the updated question bank.
- Alternative Flows: -   **A1 - Delete Question:** The Lecturer selects a question for deletion. The system checks whether deletion is permitted under BR-ASSESSMENT-006 and removes it when safe.
    -   **A2 - Search or Filter:** The Lecturer searches or filters questions by supported attributes such as topic, difficulty, or question type.
    -   **A3 - Cancel Change:** The Lecturer cancels before saving; no question data is changed.
- Exception Flows: -   **E1 - Invalid Question Data:** The system identifies missing or invalid information and requests correction.
    -   **E2 - Unauthorized Course:** The system denies access when the Lecturer is not assigned to the course.
    -   **E3 - Question Cannot Be Deleted:** The system preserves a question whose deletion would invalidate historical submitted attempts and informs the Lecturer.
- Postconditions: -   The question bank reflects successful changes without modifying historical assessment-attempt data.

### UC-ASSESSMENT-002 - Create and Configure Assessment

- Related Requirements: FR-ASSESSMENT-002, FR-ASSESSMENT-003
- Primary Actor: Lecturer
- Preconditions: -   The Lecturer is authenticated and assigned to the target course.
    -   The target course exists.
- Trigger: The Lecturer selects **Create Assessment** for the course.
- Main Flow: 1.  The system displays the assessment configuration form.
    2.  The Lecturer enters the assessment title, description, availability period, duration, maximum attempts, and grading configuration.
    3.  The Lecturer selects questions from the course question bank.
    4.  The Lecturer configures optional settings such as an access password and question/option shuffling.
    5.  The system validates the assessment configuration and total point values.
    6.  The Lecturer selects **Save and Publish**.
    7.  The system stores the assessment with `PUBLISHED` status.
    8.  The system confirms successful publication.
- Alternative Flows: -   **A1 - Save as Draft:** The Lecturer selects **Save as Draft**; the system stores the assessment with `DRAFT` status and does not make it available to Students.
    -   **A2 - Edit Draft:** The Lecturer opens an existing Draft assessment, changes its configuration, and saves it.
    -   **A3 - Cancel:** The Lecturer cancels before saving; no new assessment is created.
- Exception Flows: -   **E1 - No Questions Selected:** The system rejects publication until at least one valid question is included.
    -   **E2 - Invalid Configuration:** The system identifies invalid dates, duration, attempt limits, point values, or other configuration and requests correction.
    -   **E3 - Unauthorized Course:** The system denies the operation.
- Postconditions: -   A valid assessment is stored as `DRAFT` or `PUBLISHED`.

### UC-ASSESSMENT-003 - Take Assessment

- Related Requirements: FR-ASSESSMENT-004, FR-ASSESSMENT-005, FR-ASSESSMENT-006
- Primary Actor: Student
- Preconditions: -   The Student is authenticated with an active account.
    -   The Student has an ACTIVE enrollment in the course.
    -   The assessment is `PUBLISHED` and within its configured availability period.
    -   The Student has not exceeded the maximum number of attempts.
- Trigger: The Student selects **Start Assessment**.
- Main Flow: 1.  The system verifies enrollment, assessment availability, and remaining attempts.
    2.  The system displays the assessment overview, including duration, question count, remaining attempts, and instructions.
    3.  The Student confirms that they want to start.
    4.  The system creates a new assessment attempt, records its start time, and starts the server-authoritative assessment timer.
    5.  The system displays the assessment questions according to the configured ordering and shuffling rules.
    6.  The Student selects or enters responses.
    7.  The system periodically saves the Student's responses.
    8.  The Student selects **Submit Assessment**.
    9.  The system displays a submission confirmation.
    10. The Student confirms submission.
    11. The system records the submission time and final responses.
    12. The system automatically grades objective questions.
    13. If no manual grading is required, the system updates the attempt to `GRADED`; otherwise, it updates the attempt to `AWAITING_GRADING`.
    14. The system confirms successful submission.
- Alternative Flows: -   **A1 - Password-Protected Assessment:** Before creating the attempt, the system requests and validates the configured assessment password.
    -   **A2 - Resume Active Attempt:** If the Student returns to an existing valid in-progress attempt, the system restores saved responses and the remaining server-authoritative time.
    -   **A3 - Essay Questions Present:** The system grades objective questions but withholds the final result until required manual grading is finalized.
- Exception Flows: -   **E1 - Time Expired:** The system stops further response editing and automatically submits the latest saved responses.
    -   **E2 - Maximum Attempts Reached:** The system denies creation of another attempt.
    -   **E3 - Assessment Not Available:** The system denies access when the assessment is not published or is outside its availability period.
    -   **E4 - No ACTIVE Enrollment:** The system denies the attempt.
    -   **E5 - Temporary Connection Loss:** The client preserves unsynchronized responses locally where supported and synchronizes them when connectivity returns while the attempt remains valid; server time remains authoritative.
- Postconditions: -   A submitted attempt and its responses are stored.
    -   Objective responses are graded automatically.
    -   Assessment attempt and result data are available to authorized modules, including Learning Analytics, without this module calculating a risk score.

### UC-ASSESSMENT-004 - Grade Essay Assessment

- Related Requirements: FR-ASSESSMENT-007, FR-ASSESSMENT-008
- Primary Actor: Lecturer
- Preconditions: -   The Lecturer is authenticated and assigned to the course.
    -   At least one submitted assessment attempt contains an essay response awaiting grading.
- Trigger: The Lecturer opens a submission with `AWAITING_GRADING` status.
- Main Flow: 1.  The system verifies the Lecturer's course permission.
    2.  The system displays submissions awaiting manual grading.
    3.  The Lecturer selects a Student submission.
    4.  The system displays the essay questions and submitted responses.
    5.  The Lecturer assigns scores and enters feedback.
    6.  The Lecturer selects **Finalize Grading**.
    7.  The system validates all manually assigned scores against their configured point limits.
    8.  The system calculates the final assessment score.
    9.  The system stores the scores and feedback and changes the attempt status to `GRADED`.
    10. The result becomes available according to the configured result-release policy.
- Alternative Flows: -   **A1 - Save Grading Draft:** The Lecturer saves current grading progress without finalizing; the attempt remains pending final grading.
- Exception Flows: -   **E1 - Invalid Score:** The system rejects a score outside the allowed range and requests correction.
    -   **E2 - Unauthorized Course:** The system denies access to the submission.
    -   **E3 - Attempt Already Finalized:** The system prevents an unauthorized overwrite of a finalized result.
- Postconditions: -   On successful finalization, essay scores, feedback, and the final assessment score are stored.
    -   Finalized assessment data become available to Learning Analytics as input data; risk calculation remains the responsibility of Learning Analytics.

### UC-ASSESSMENT-005 - View Assessment Result

- Related Requirements: FR-ASSESSMENT-008
- Primary Actor: Student
- Preconditions: -   The Student is authenticated.
    -   The Student owns the requested assessment attempt.
    -   The result is available under the assessment's result-release policy.
- Trigger: The Student selects a completed assessment or assessment attempt.
- Main Flow: 1.  The system verifies that the requested attempt belongs to the Student.
    2.  The system checks the result-release policy.
    3.  The system retrieves the released assessment result.
    4.  The system displays the final score and attempt information.
    5.  The system displays answer details and Lecturer feedback when the release policy permits.
- Alternative Flows: -   **A1 - Multiple Attempts:** The Student selects a previous attempt and the system displays its released result.
    -   **A2 - Limited Result Release:** The system displays only the information permitted by the configured release policy.
- Exception Flows: -   **E1 - Result Not Yet Released:** The system informs the Student that the result is not yet available.
    -   **E2 - Unauthorized Attempt:** The system denies access to another Student's result.
- Postconditions: -   No assessment data is changed.
    -   No risk score, risk level, risk factor, or contributing risk indicator is exposed to the Student.

### UC-ASSESSMENT-006 - View Assessment Performance

- Related Requirements: FR-ASSESSMENT-009
- Primary Actor: Lecturer, Administrator
- Preconditions: -   The actor is authenticated and authorized for the requested assessment information.
    -   Assessment attempt data exists.
- Trigger: The actor opens assessment performance information.
- Main Flow: 1.  The system verifies the actor's authorization.
    2.  The system retrieves authorized assessment attempts and results.
    3.  The system calculates assessment-level descriptive statistics such as submission count, completion rate, and score distribution or averages.
    4.  The system displays the assessment performance information.
- Alternative Flows: -   **A1 - Filter Results:** The actor applies supported course, assessment, or attempt filters and the system refreshes the displayed statistics.
- Exception Flows: -   **E1 - No Assessment Data:** The system displays an empty state.
    -   **E2 - Unauthorized Request:** The system denies access.
- Postconditions: -   No assessment data is modified.

## 5. Business Rules
### BR-ASSESSMENT-001 - Assessment Availability

- Description: A Student may start an assessment only when it is `PUBLISHED`, the current server time is within its configured availability period, the Student has an ACTIVE enrollment in the course, and the Student has not reached the maximum number of attempts.

### BR-ASSESSMENT-002 - Time Limit

- Description: The assessment timer is based on server-authoritative time. When the configured duration expires, the system must prevent further response changes and submit the latest stored responses.

### BR-ASSESSMENT-003 - Maximum Attempt Limit

- Description: A Student may create no more than the configured maximum number of attempts for an assessment. The assessment configuration must define how multiple attempts contribute to the official result when multiple attempts are allowed, such as highest, average, or latest attempt.

### BR-ASSESSMENT-004 - Periodic Response Saving

- Description: During an active assessment attempt, the system must periodically persist Student responses. Temporary client-side recovery may be used during short connection failures, but the server remains authoritative for attempt state and timing.

### BR-ASSESSMENT-005 - Question and Option Shuffling

- Description: When question or option randomization is enabled, the system must generate the applicable ordering for each attempt without changing the semantic content or correct answer definition.

### BR-ASSESSMENT-006 - Historical Attempt Integrity

- Description: Changes to questions or assessment configuration must not corrupt or retroactively alter the question content, submitted responses, scores, or grading evidence associated with historical submitted attempts. The implementation must preserve the information required to reproduce an authorized historical result.

### BR-ASSESSMENT-007 - Grading Constraints

- Description: Automatically graded questions must use the answer key and point values applicable to the attempt. Manually assigned essay scores must be within the range from zero to the configured maximum points for the question.

### BR-ASSESSMENT-008 - Result Release

- Description: Assessment results, answer details, and Lecturer feedback are visible to a Student only according to the assessment's configured release policy. A result requiring manual grading must not be presented as a final result before grading is finalized.

### BR-ASSESSMENT-009 - Assessment Data Privacy

- Description: A Student may access only their own authorized assessment attempts and released results. A Lecturer may access assessment data only for assigned courses. An Administrator may access only authorized system-level information. One Student's assessment data must not be disclosed to another Student.

### BR-ASSESSMENT-010 - Learning Analytics Boundary

- Description: Assessment provides authorized attempt and result data to Learning Analytics. Learning Analytics, not Assessment, owns normalization of risk indicators, team-defined weighted-sum risk-score calculation, risk classification, risk factors, and early-warning logic. Risk scores, risk levels, risk factors, and contributing risk indicators must never be exposed to Students.

# Interaction & Notification

## 1. Overview
- This module provides an interaction channel (per-lesson discussion/forum) and a notification system for important events: new content, submission deadlines, grading results, discussion replies, and intervention alerts from the Learning Analytics module (07).

## 2. Actors
- Student
- Lecturer
- Admin

## 3. Functional Requirements
### FR-INT-001 - Post a Question/Comment on a Lesson
- Description: A student can post a question/comment attached to a specific lesson.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-INT-002 - Reply to a Discussion Thread
- Description: A student or lecturer can reply to an existing question/comment.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-INT-003 - Report Inappropriate Content
- Description: Any user can report a post/comment as inappropriate, along with a reason.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-INT-004 - Moderate Reported Content
- Description: The lecturer (within their own course) or Admin (system-wide) reviews reported content and hides/deletes it or dismisses the report.
- Priority: Should-have

### FR-INT-005 - Notify on New Content / Deadline / Grading Result
- Description: The system sends notifications when a lecturer posts new content, when a submission deadline is approaching, and when a submission has been graded.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-INT-006 - Notification on Forum Reply
- Description: When someone replies to a thread that a user follows/has posted in, that user receives a notification.
- Priority: Should-have

### FR-INT-007 - Lecturer Sends Targeted Intervention Notification
- Description: From the Learning Analytics dashboard (07), the lecturer can send a direct reminder/support message to at-risk students; the message is delivered through the notification system.
- Priority: Should-have

### FR-INT-008 - Manage Notifications
- Description: Users can view their list of notifications and mark them as read.
- Priority: Should-have

2. The system validates and saves the reply.
3. The system pushes a notification to thread participants.
- Exception Flows: The thread has been deleted/hidden â†’ reject with a notice. Empty content â†’ validation error.

### UC-INT-003 - Report Inappropriate Content
- Related Requirements: FR-INT-003

- Trigger: The user clicks "Report".

2. The system records the report and flags the content for moderation.

- Description: A user may create at most N posts/replies per minute (e.g., 5) to limit spam.

# Learning Analytics

## 1. Overview
- This module is a **mandatory advanced component** of the project (Direction 5). It ingests learning behavior data and assessment results, computes a risk score and risk level for each student per course, explains the contributing factors (risk factors), displays them on a lecturer dashboard, and supports the lecturer in taking intervention actions.
- MVP scope: a rule-based baseline model, a lecturer dashboard, and evaluation on simulated student data. Out of MVP scope: an actual ML model (only to be done if sufficient labeled data is available).

## 2. Actors
- Lecturer (primary user)
- Admin (course-level/system-level aggregate statistics)

## 3. Functional Requirements
### FR-ANL-001 - Collect Learning Indicators
- Description: The system aggregates raw data from `LearningActivity` (module 04) and `Assessment` (module 05) into indicators per student/course, on a predefined cycle.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ANL-002 - Compute Risk Score
- Description: The system computes a numeric risk score for each student/course using a weighted-sum formula over the collected indicators.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ANL-003 - Classify Risk Level
- Description: The system maps the risk score to a Low / Medium / High level based on configurable thresholds.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ANL-004 - Generate Risk Factor Explanations
- Description: For each risk assessment, the system stores the top contributing factors (e.g., "3 missed deadlines", "no login in 10 days") so the lecturer understands why a student was flagged.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ANL-005 - Lecturer Risk Dashboard
- Description: The lecturer views a list of students (filterable/sortable) with their current risk level, trend, and last update time, per course.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ANL-006 - Lecturer Views Student Risk Details
- Description: The lecturer can drill down into an individual student to see the history/trend of their risk score and an analysis of the risk factors.
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ANL-007 - Trigger Intervention
- Description: The lecturer can send a reminder/support message directly to a flagged student from the dashboard (integrated with FR-INT-007, module 06).
- Priority: Must-have

### FR-ANL-008 - Log Intervention Outcome
- Description: The system records that an intervention was sent and (optionally) tracks whether the risk score improves afterward.
- Priority: Should-have

### FR-ANL-009 - Course-Level Aggregate Analytics
- Description: Admin/lecturer can view course-level statistics: enrollment count, completion rate, average score, and the percentage of students at each risk level.
- Priority: Should-have

### FR-ANL-010 - Evaluate Against Simulated Profiles
- Description: The system supports running the risk model against a set of simulated student profiles with expected labels, in order to validate and report on model effectiveness (a mandatory requirement of the assignment).
- Priority: Must-have (mandatory for the report/demo)

## 4. Use Cases
### UC-ANL-001 - Lecturer Views At-Risk Student Dashboard
- Related Requirements: FR-ANL-005
- Primary Actor: Lecturer
- Preconditions: A risk assessment already exists for the course.
- Trigger: The Analytics tab of the course is opened.
- Main Flow: 1. The system retrieves the latest `RiskAssessment` for each student.
2. It displays the list sorted by risk level (High first) with filters available.
- Postconditions: None (read-only).

### UC-ANL-002 - Lecturer Views Risk Explanation
- Related Requirements: FR-ANL-004, FR-ANL-006
- Primary Actor: Lecturer
- Preconditions: A `RiskAssessment` exists for the selected student.
- Trigger: The lecturer clicks on a student row.
- Main Flow: 1. A trend chart of the score over time is displayed.
2. A list of risk factors with their values is displayed (e.g., "Logins: 0 times in the last 14 days").
- Postconditions: None.

### UC-ANL-003 - Lecturer Sends an Intervention
- Related Requirements: FR-ANL-007, FR-ANL-008
- Primary Actor: Lecturer
- Preconditions: The student is at Medium/High risk level.
- Trigger: The lecturer clicks "Send Reminder".
- Main Flow: 1. The lecturer selects/writes a message.
2. The system creates an `Intervention` record linked to the `RiskAssessment` and sends it through the notification module.
3. At the next scoring cycle, the system may compare the risk score before and after.
- Postconditions: The intervention is recorded.

## 5. Business Rules
### BR-ANL-001 - Scoring Frequency
- Description: The risk score is recomputed daily (a nightly batch job), with an option to recompute manually on demand.

### BR-ANL-002 - Weighted-Sum Risk Model
- Description: The risk score is calculated from normalized risk indicators using `RiskScore = Î£(w_i Ã— r_i)`, where `r_i` is a normalized risk indicator in [0,100] and `w_i` is the team-defined non-negative weight for indicator `i`. The weights must sum to 1 and must be applied consistently to students evaluated under the same model version.

### BR-ANL-003 - Risk Thresholds
- Description: The risk score ranges over [0,100]. The current thresholds are 0â€“39 = Low, 40â€“69 = Medium, 70â€“100 = High; they may be calibrated using the simulated-profile evaluation before the final model version is fixed.

### BR-ANL-004 - Cold-Start Handling
- Description: Students enrolled for fewer than X days, or who have insufficient data (e.g., fewer than 2 recorded learning sessions), are shown "Insufficient data" instead of being assigned a risk level, to avoid false positives.

### BR-ANL-005 - Explainability Requirement
- Description: Every `RiskAssessment` must be traceable to at least one `RiskFactor` with a human-readable description; a raw score without an explanation does not satisfy the rubric requirement for "explanation and intervention action".

### BR-ANL-006 - Privacy/Ethical Use
- Description: Risk scores, risk levels, risk factors, and contributing risk indicators are visible only to the lecturer responsible for that course and to authorized Admins. Students cannot access their own or another student's risk assessment data. The use of behavioral data for this purpose must be clearly disclosed.

# Database Conventions and Migration Rules

## 1. Purpose

This document defines the shared database conventions for the Smart Campus LMS backend.

The ERD is the conceptual/logical reference for entities and relationships.
Flyway migration files are the executable history of the physical database schema.
After `V1__init_schema.sql` is accepted and merged, V1 is treated as the baseline and must not be edited.

## 2. Technology

- Database: MySQL 8.4
- Schema migration: Flyway
- Persistence: Spring Data JPA / JPA / Hibernate
- Hibernate schema policy: `ddl-auto=validate`
- Database naming: `snake_case`
- Java naming: `camelCase`

## 3. Primary Keys

Standalone entities use:

```sql
id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY
```

Java entities should therefore normally use:

```java
private Long id;
```

Pure join tables may use composite primary keys where defined by the ERD.

## 4. Foreign Keys and Role Validation

Foreign keys guarantee that the referenced record exists.

They do NOT guarantee application roles. For example:

- `student_id -> users.id` does not prove that the user has role `STUDENT`.
- `lecturer_id -> users.id` does not prove that the user has role `LECTURER`.

Role-specific rules are validated in the Spring service/security layer.

## 5. Application Enums

Application states are stored as `VARCHAR`, not MySQL `ENUM`.

Examples:

- User role: `STUDENT`, `LECTURER`, `ADMIN`
- User status: `ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE`
- Course publication state: `DRAFT`, `PUBLISHED`, `ARCHIVED`
- Enrollment status: `ACTIVE`, `COMPLETED`, `DROPPED`
- Assessment status: `DRAFT`, `PUBLISHED`, `CLOSED`
- Attempt status: `IN_PROGRESS`, `SUBMITTED`, `GRADED`
- Risk level: `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH`
- Intervention status: `OPEN`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `COMPLETED`, `CANCELLED`

Java should map these values using string enum mapping, for example:

```java
@Enumerated(EnumType.STRING)
private Role role;
```

Database `CHECK` constraints may enforce stable enum values.

## 6. Uniqueness Rules

The baseline enforces these important rules:

- `users.username` is unique.
- `users.email` is unique.
- One enrollment per `(student_id, course_id)`.
- One learning-progress record per `(student_id, lesson_id)`.
- One attempt number per `(assessment_id, student_id, attempt_number)`.
- One answer per `(attempt_id, question_id)`.
- Chapter `order_index` is unique within a course.
- Lesson `order_index` is unique within a chapter.
- Assessment-question `order_index` is unique within an assessment.

These constraints protect invariants even if application code has a bug or concurrent requests occur.

## 7. Delete Strategy

Do not physically delete users merely to deactivate an account. Use `users.status`.

Do not physically delete a course merely to stop publication. Use `courses.publication_state = 'ARCHIVED'` when appropriate.

Default policy for historical or learning records is `ON DELETE RESTRICT`.

`ON DELETE CASCADE` is reserved for records that are strongly owned by their parent, such as:

- `course_lecturers` when its course is deleted.
- chapters when their course is physically deleted.
- lessons when their chapter is physically deleted.
- learning materials when their lesson is physically deleted.
- `assessment_questions` when its assessment is deleted.
- attempt answers when their attempt is deleted.
- risk factors when their risk assessment is deleted.

A physical deletion that is blocked by `RESTRICT` must be handled explicitly by business logic rather than by weakening the foreign key casually.

## 8. Timestamp Strategy

Database timestamps use MySQL defaults.

For creation timestamps:

```sql
created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
```

For mutable records:

```sql
updated_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL
    DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
    ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
```

Application code should not depend on nullable creation timestamps.

## 9. Scores and Numeric Precision

Do not use `FLOAT` for persisted scores or assessment points.

Use `DECIMAL`, for example:

```sql
score DECIMAL(8,2)
```

Risk score uses:

```sql
risk_score DECIMAL(5,2)
```

with range `0..100`.

Java should normally use `BigDecimal` for these fields.

## 10. Question and Answer Data

`question_bank.answer_data` and `attempt_answers.answer_data` use MySQL `JSON`.

This allows different answer structures for different question types without adding many nullable columns.

Initial question types:

- `SINGLE_CHOICE`
- `MULTIPLE_CHOICE`
- `TRUE_FALSE`
- `SHORT_ANSWER`

The Assessment module owner must define and document the JSON contract used by each question type before implementing serialization/deserialization.

## 11. Learning Activity and Progress

`learning_activities.lesson_id` is nullable because some learning events may not belong to a specific lesson.

`event_type` remains a `VARCHAR` so the application can evolve the event vocabulary. Event names should still be defined centrally in Java rather than scattered as string literals.

`last_position`, `current_position`, and `total_length` are non-negative integer position fields.

IMPORTANT OPEN CONTRACT:
The team must finalize the exact semantic/unit of these position fields before implementing progress tracking for multiple content types. For video/audio they may represent seconds; other lesson types may require a different interpretation.

A schema change discovered later must be introduced by a new Flyway migration rather than by editing an already-shared V1.

## 12. Learning Analytics

Risk assessments are historical snapshots, not a single overwritten current row.

Initial risk levels:

- `LOW`
- `MEDIUM`
- `HIGH`

Initial risk score range:

```text
0 <= risk_score <= 100
```

The risk-scoring formula, weights, thresholds, and factor calculation are application/business rules and belong primarily in the analytics service. They are not hard-coded into V1 except for the persisted score range and risk-level vocabulary.

Risk factors belong to one risk assessment.

Interventions reference the risk assessment that motivated the intervention and the user who created it.

## 13. Indexing

Indexes should support actual query patterns rather than being added to every column.

The baseline explicitly adds indexes for common/high-volume access patterns such as:

- learning activities by student and time
- learning activities by lesson and time
- assessment attempts by student
- risk assessments by student/course/time
- risk assessments by course/risk level

Primary keys, unique constraints, and MySQL foreign-key requirements already provide or require indexes in several other places.

Additional indexes should be justified by real queries or performance measurements.

## 14. Flyway Rules

`V1__init_schema.sql` is the initial database baseline.

Before V1 is accepted by the team, it may be corrected while the development database is disposable.

After V1 is merged/shared and used by the team:

1. Never edit, rename, or delete V1.
2. Every schema change gets a new versioned migration.
3. Never use Hibernate `ddl-auto=create` or `ddl-auto=update` as the team schema-management mechanism.
4. Use Hibernate `ddl-auto=validate`.
5. Never make an untracked manual schema change in MySQL and assume teammates will reproduce it.
6. Database objects such as tables, constraints, indexes, views, triggers, procedures, and functions must be created/changed through Flyway when they are part of the application schema.
7. Before merging a PR containing a migration, update/rebase from `main` and ensure the migration version is not duplicated.
8. Test migrations from a clean database when practical.
9. Once a migration has been merged/applied as shared history, fix mistakes with a later migration instead of rewriting history.

Example:

```text
V1__init_schema.sql
V2__add_course_thumbnail.sql
V3__add_activity_event_index.sql
V4__create_some_database_object.sql
```

Parallel backend work is allowed. Migration version conflicts are resolved before merging to `main`.

## 15. Application Layer Responsibilities

Flyway owns schema evolution.

JPA/Hibernate maps Java objects to the existing schema.

Spring services own most business workflows and validations.

The database should enforce structural/data-integrity invariants such as:

- primary keys
- foreign keys
- uniqueness
- nullability
- stable checks
- appropriate numeric ranges

Business rules such as authorization, role-specific actions, enrollment workflows, risk-score calculation, and intervention behavior normally belong in the application service/security layer.

## 16. Open Decisions Before Relevant Feature Implementation

The following details are intentionally not invented by the database baseline and must be finalized by the responsible module owner before implementation:

1. Exact semantics/units for lesson progress position fields across all content types.
2. Exact JSON schema for `question_bank.answer_data` and `attempt_answers.answer_data`.
3. Complete vocabulary for `learning_activities.event_type`.
4. Complete vocabulary for `lessons.content_type` and `learning_materials.file_type`.
5. Complete vocabulary for `risk_factors.factor_type`.
6. Complete vocabulary for `interventions.intervention_type`.

If one of these decisions requires a physical schema change after V1 has been shared, create V2/V3/etc.; do not edit V1.

import type { DiscussionComment, DiscussionPayload } from './discussion.type'
import { getApi, postApi, putApi, deleteApi } from '~/config/axiosClient'

export const getCourseDiscussions = (courseId: number) => getApi<DiscussionComment[]>(`/courses/${courseId}/discussions`)

export const createDiscussionComment = (
  courseId: number,
  payload: DiscussionPayload,
) => 
  postApi<DiscussionComment>(`/courses/${courseId}/discussions`, payload)

export const updateDiscussionComment = (
  courseId: number,
  id: number,
  payload: DiscussionPayload
) => 
  putApi<DiscussionComment>(`/courses/${courseId}/discussions/${id}`, payload)

export const deleteDiscussionComment = (courseId: number, id: number) => deleteApi(`/courses/${courseId}/discussions/${id}`)

import { skipToken, useMutation, useQuery, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import {
  createDiscussionComment,
  deleteDiscussionComment,
  getCourseDiscussions,
  updateDiscussionComment,
} from './discussion.api'
import type { DiscussionPayload } from './discussion.type'

const discussionQueryKey = (courseId: number) => ['discussions', courseId] as const

export const useGetCourseDiscussions = (courseId?: number) =>
  useQuery({
    queryKey: ['discussions', courseId],
    queryFn: courseId === undefined ? skipToken : () => getCourseDiscussions(courseId),
  })

export const useCreateDiscussionComment = (courseId?: number) => {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()

  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: (payload: DiscussionPayload ) => createDiscussionComment(courseId!, payload),
    onSuccess: () =>
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: discussionQueryKey(courseId!) }),
  })
}

export const useUpdateDiscussionComment = (courseId?: number) => {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()

  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: (payload: {
      id: number
      content: string
      parentId?: number
    }) => updateDiscussionComment(courseId!, payload.id, {
      content: payload.content,
      parentId: payload.parentId
    }),
    onSuccess: () =>
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: discussionQueryKey(courseId!) }),
  })
}

export const useDeleteDiscussionComment = (courseId?: number) => {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()

  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: (id: number) => deleteDiscussionComment(courseId!, id),
    onSuccess: () =>
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: discussionQueryKey(courseId!) }),
  })
}

import { useEffect, useMemo, useState } from 'react'
import type { FormEvent, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { useTranslation } from 'react-i18next'
import { FontAwesomeIcon } from '@fortawesome/react-fontawesome'
import { faPaperPlane } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'
import {
  useCreateDiscussionComment,
  useDeleteDiscussionComment,
  useGetCourseDiscussions,
  useUpdateDiscussionComment,
} from './services/discussion.query'
import type { DiscussionComment } from './services/discussion.type'

type SortOrder = 'newest' | 'oldest'

type DiscussProps = {
  courseId?: number
}

const EMPTY_COMMENTS: DiscussionComment[] = []

const formatDate = (value: string, language: string) => {
  const date = new Date(value)
  if (Number.isNaN(date.getTime())) return value

  return new Intl.DateTimeFormat(language === 'vi' ? 'vi-VN' : 'en-US', {
    dateStyle: 'medium',
    timeStyle: 'short',
  }).format(date)
}

const getInitials = (name: string) =>
  name
    .trim()
    .split(/\s+/)
    .slice(-2)
    .map((part) => part[0])
    .join('')
    .toLocaleUpperCase()

export default function Discuss({ courseId }: Readonly<DiscussProps>) {
  const { t, i18n } = useTranslation('discussion')
  const [sortOrder, setSortOrder] = useState<SortOrder>('newest')
  const [newContent, setNewContent] = useState('')
  const [replyToId, setReplyToId] = useState<number | null>(null)
  const [replyContent, setReplyContent] = useState('')
  const [editingId, setEditingId] = useState<number | null>(null)
  const [editContent, setEditContent] = useState('')

  // Reset tráº¡ng thÃ¡i reply/edit khi chuyá»ƒn sang khÃ³a há»c khÃ¡c
  useEffect(() => {
    setNewContent('')
    setReplyToId(null)
    setReplyContent('')
    setEditingId(null)
    setEditContent('')
  }, [courseId])

  const discussionsQuery = useGetCourseDiscussions(courseId)
  const createComment = useCreateDiscussionComment(courseId)
  const updateComment = useUpdateDiscussionComment(courseId)
  const deleteComment = useDeleteDiscussionComment(courseId)
  const comments = Array.isArray(discussionsQuery.data)
    ? discussionsQuery.data
    : EMPTY_COMMENTS

  const roots = useMemo(() => {
    return comments
      .filter((comment) => comment.parentId === null)
      .sort((left, right) => {
        const difference =
          new Date(left.createdAt).getTime() - new Date(right.createdAt).getTime()
        return sortOrder === 'newest' ? -difference : difference
      })
  }, [comments, sortOrder])

  const submitComment = (event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>, parentId?: number) => {
    event.preventDefault()

    const content = (parentId === undefined ? newContent : replyContent).trim()
    if (!content) return

    createComment.mutate({ content, parentId },
      {
        onSuccess: () => {
          if (parentId === undefined) setNewContent('')
          else {
            setReplyContent('')
            setReplyToId(null)
          }
        },
      },
    )
  }

  const submitEdit = (event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>, id: number) => {
    event.preventDefault()
    if (!editContent.trim()) return

    updateComment.mutate(
      { id: id, content: editContent.trim() },
      {
        onSuccess: () => {
          setEditingId(null)
          setEditContent('')
        },
      },
    )
  }

  const removeComment = (id: number) => {
    if (!window.confirm(t('confirm_delete'))) return
    deleteComment.mutate(id)
  }

  const renderComment = (comment: DiscussionComment, depth = 0): ReactNode => {
    const replies = comments
      .filter((candidate) => candidate.parentId === comment.id)
      .sort(
        (left, right) =>
          new Date(left.createdAt).getTime() - new Date(right.createdAt).getTime(),
      )
    const isEditing = editingId === comment.id
    return (
      <article
        key={comment.id}
        className={`rounded-xl border border-border/60 bg-white p-4 shadow-xs dark:bg-surface md:p-5 ${
          depth > 0 ? 'ml-4 border-l-2 border-l-primary/30' : ''
        }`}
      >
        <div className="flex items-start gap-3">
          <div className="grid h-10 w-10 shrink-0 place-items-center rounded-full bg-primary-soft text-xs font-bold text-primary">
            {getInitials(comment.authorName)}
          </div>
          <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
            <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-2">
              <div>
                <p className="font-semibold text-sm text-fg">{comment.authorName}</p>
                <time
                  dateTime={comment.createdAt}
                  className="text-xs text-fg-subtle"
                >
                  {formatDate(comment.createdAt, i18n.language)}
                </time>
              </div>
              {!comment.deleted && (
                <div className="flex items-center gap-3 text-xs font-semibold">
                  <button
                    type="button"
                    onClick={() => {
                      setReplyToId(comment.id)
                      setReplyContent('')
                      setEditingId(null)
                    }}
                    className="text-primary hover:underline"
                  >
                    {t('reply')}
                  </button>
                  <button
                    type="button"
                    onClick={() => {
                      setEditingId(comment.id)
                      setEditContent(comment.content)
                      setReplyToId(null)
                    }}
                    className="text-fg-muted hover:text-primary"
                  >
                    {t('edit')}
                  </button>
                  <button
                    type="button"
                    onClick={() => removeComment(comment.id)}
                    disabled={deleteComment.isPending}
                    className="text-red-600 hover:underline disabled:opacity-50"
                  >
                    {t('delete')}
                  </button>
                </div>
              )}
            </div>

            {isEditing ? (
              <form
                onSubmit={(event) => submitEdit(event, comment.id)}
                className="mt-3 flex flex-col gap-2"
              >
                <textarea
                  value={editContent}
                  onChange={(event) => setEditContent(event.target.value)}
                  maxLength={5000}
                  required
                  aria-label={t('edit_placeholder')}
                  className="min-h-20 w-full resize-y rounded-lg border border-border bg-surface-muted px-3 py-2 text-sm text-fg focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-primary"
                />
                <div className="flex justify-end gap-2">
                  <button
                    type="button"
                    onClick={() => setEditingId(null)}
                    className="rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-xs font-semibold text-fg-muted hover:bg-surface-muted"
                  >
                    {t('cancel')}
                  </button>
                  <button
                    type="submit"
                    disabled={!editContent.trim() || updateComment.isPending}
                    className="rounded-lg bg-primary px-3 py-2 text-xs font-semibold text-on-primary disabled:opacity-50"
                  >
                    {t('save')}
                  </button>
                </div>
              </form>
            ) : (
              <p className="mt-3 whitespace-pre-wrap text-sm leading-relaxed text-fg">
                {comment.deleted ? t('deleted_comment') : comment.content}
              </p>
            )}

            {replyToId === comment.id && (
              <form
                onSubmit={(event) => submitComment(event, comment.id)}
                className="mt-3 flex flex-col gap-2"
              >
                <textarea
                  value={replyContent}
                  onChange={(event) => setReplyContent(event.target.value)}
                  placeholder={t('reply_placeholder')}
                  maxLength={5000}
                  required
                  className="min-h-20 w-full resize-y rounded-lg border border-border bg-surface-muted px-3 py-2 text-sm text-fg placeholder:text-fg-subtle focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-primary"
                />
                <div className="flex justify-end gap-2">
                  <button
                    type="button"
                    onClick={() => setReplyToId(null)}
                    className="rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-xs font-semibold text-fg-muted hover:bg-surface-muted"
                  >
                    {t('cancel')}
                  </button>
                  <button
                    type="submit"
                    disabled={!replyContent.trim() || createComment.isPending}
                    className="rounded-lg bg-primary px-3 py-2 text-xs font-semibold text-on-primary disabled:opacity-50"
                  >
                    {t('reply')}
                  </button>
                </div>
              </form>
            )}
          </div>
        </div>
        {replies.length > 0 && (
          <div className="mt-4 flex flex-col gap-3">
            {replies.map((reply) => renderComment(reply, depth + 1))}
          </div>
        )}
      </article>
    )
  }

  const mutationError = createComment.error ?? updateComment.error ?? deleteComment.error

  return (
    <div className="flex h-full min-h-[calc(100vh-112px)] w-full flex-col overflow-hidden">
      <section className="flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col overflow-hidden rounded-xl bg-white dark:bg-surface">
        <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-4 border-b border-border px-4 py-4 md:px-8">
          <h1 className="font-['Be_Vietnam_Pro'] text-xl font-semibold tracking-tight text-fg">
            {t('title')}
          </h1>
          <label className="flex items-center gap-2 text-xs font-semibold text-fg-muted">
            <span>{t('sort_by')}</span>
            <select
              value={sortOrder}
              onChange={(event) =>
                setSortOrder(event.target.value === 'oldest' ? 'oldest' : 'newest')
              }
              className="rounded-lg border border-border bg-surface px-2.5 py-2 text-sm text-fg"
            >
              <option value="newest">{t('sort_newest')}</option>
              <option value="oldest">{t('sort_oldest')}</option>
            </select>
          </label>
        </div>

        <div className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto bg-[#FAF8FF] px-4 py-5 dark:bg-surface-muted/30 md:px-8">
          {discussionsQuery.isLoading ? (
            <p className="p-5 text-center text-sm text-fg-muted">{t('loading_comments')}</p>
          ) : discussionsQuery.isError ? (
            <div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-3 rounded-xl border border-border bg-surface p-6 text-center">
              <p role="alert" className="text-sm text-fg-muted">
                {discussionsQuery.error.message || t('comments_error')}
              </p>
              <button
                type="button"
                onClick={() => discussionsQuery.refetch()}
                className="rounded-lg bg-primary px-4 py-2 text-sm font-semibold text-on-primary"
              >
                {t('retry')}
              </button>
            </div>
          ) : roots.length === 0 ? (
            <p className="rounded-xl border border-dashed border-border bg-surface p-8 text-center text-sm text-fg-muted">
              {t('no_comments')}
            </p>
          ) : (
            <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
              {roots.map((comment) => renderComment(comment))}
            </div>
          )}
        </div>

        <form
          onSubmit={(event) => submitComment(event)}
          className="border-t border-border bg-white p-4 shadow-[0px_-4px_16px_rgba(0,0,0,0.03)] dark:bg-surface md:p-5"
        >
          {mutationError && (
            <p role="alert" className="mb-3 text-sm text-red-600">
              {mutationError.message || t('submit_error')}
            </p>
          )}
          <label htmlFor="new-discussion" className="sr-only">
            {t('placeholder')}
          </label>
          <div className="flex items-end gap-3">
            <textarea
              id="new-discussion"
              value={newContent}
              onChange={(event) => setNewContent(event.target.value)}
              placeholder={t('placeholder')}
              maxLength={5000}
              required
              className="min-h-20 flex-1 resize-y rounded-xl bg-surface-muted px-3.5 py-3 text-sm text-fg placeholder:text-fg-subtle focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-primary"
            />
            <button
              type="submit"
              disabled={!newContent.trim() || createComment.isPending}
              className="flex shrink-0 items-center gap-2 rounded-xl bg-primary px-4 py-3 text-sm font-semibold text-on-primary transition-colors hover:bg-primary-hover disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50"
            >
              <span>{t('submit')}</span>
              <FontAwesomeIcon icon={faPaperPlane} className="h-3 w-3" />
            </button>
          </div>
        </form>
      </section>
    </div>
  )
}

interface NotificationModalProps {
    isOpen: boolean
    onClose: () => void
}

type FilterTab = 'all' | 'courses' | 'discussion' | 'unread'

export default function NotificationModal({ isOpen, onClose }: NotificationModalProps) {
    const { t } = useTranslation()
    const navigate = useNavigate()
    const toast = useToast()
    const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = useState<FilterTab>('all')
    const isAuthenticated = Boolean(accessTokenStorage.getAccessToken())
    const notificationsQuery = useGetMyNotifications(isOpen && isAuthenticated)
    const markAsReadMutation = useMarkNotificationAsRead()
    const markAllAsReadMutation = useMarkAllNotificationsAsRead()

    if (!isOpen) return null

    const notifications = notificationsQuery.data?.filter(item => {
        if (activeTab === 'courses') {
            return ['ENROLLED_BY_STAFF', 'REMOVED_FROM_COURSE', 'COURSE_COMPLETED', 'NEW_CONTENT'].includes(item.type)
        }
        if (activeTab === 'discussion') return item.type === 'FORUM_REPLY'
        if (activeTab === 'unread') return !item.read
        return true
    }) ?? []
    const allNotifications = notificationsQuery.data ?? []
    const courseNotificationCount = allNotifications.filter(item =>
        ['ENROLLED_BY_STAFF', 'REMOVED_FROM_COURSE', 'COURSE_COMPLETED', 'NEW_CONTENT'].includes(item.type)
    ).length
    const discussionNotificationCount = allNotifications.filter(item => item.type === 'FORUM_REPLY').length
    const unreadNotificationCount = allNotifications.filter(item => !item.read).length

    const handleNotificationClick = async (item: (typeof allNotifications)[number]) => {
        if (!item.read) {
            try {
                await markAsReadMutation.mutateAsync(item.id)
            } catch (error) {
                toast.error(getErrorMessage(error, 'KhÃ´ng thá»ƒ cáº­p nháº­t tráº¡ng thÃ¡i thÃ´ng bÃ¡o.'))
                return
            }
        }
        if (item.link) navigate(item.link)
    }

    return (
        <div className="fixed inset-x-0 top-16 bottom-16 md:bottom-auto md:top-16 md:right-6 md:left-auto z-40 flex justify-end pointer-events-none">
            
            {/* Backdrop */}
            <div 
                className="fixed inset-x-0 md:inset-0 z-0 pointer-events-auto bg-transparent top-16 bottom-16 md:top-0 md:bottom-0 md:bg-black/20 md:backdrop-blur-xs transition-opacity"
                onClick={onClose}
            ></div>

            {/* Notification Main Container */}
            <div className="relative z-10 w-full h-full md:w-[576px] md:max-w-[576px] md:h-[88vh] md:max-h-[976px] bg-surface dark:bg-surface md:rounded-2xl shadow-2xl border-t md:border border-border flex flex-col overflow-hidden pointer-events-auto animate-in fade-in slide-in-from-bottom-2 md:slide-in-from-right-4 duration-200">
                
                {/* Header & Filter Tabs Section */}
                <div className="flex flex-col px-4 md:px-6 pt-3 md:pt-6 pb-3 gap-3 bg-surface dark:bg-surface border-b border-border shrink-0">
                    
                    {/* Header Title (Desktop) */}
                    <div className="hidden md:flex items-center justify-between w-full">
                        <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
                            <div className="w-9 h-9 flex items-center justify-center bg-primary-soft dark:bg-primary/20 text-primary rounded-xl shrink-0">
                                <FontAwesomeIcon icon={faBell} className="w-4 h-4" />
                            </div>
                            <h2 className="font-sans font-semibold text-xl tracking-tight text-fg">
                                {t('notifications.title', 'ThÃ´ng bÃ¡o há»‡ thá»‘ng')}
                            </h2>
                        </div>
                        <button 
                            onClick={onClose}
                            className="w-9 h-9 flex items-center justify-center rounded-xl hover:bg-surface-muted text-fg-muted transition-colors cursor-pointer"
                        >
                            <FontAwesomeIcon icon={faXmark} className="w-4 h-4" />

  onCloseNotification?: () => void
}

type ActiveItem = "trang-chu" | "khoa-hoc" | "bai-kiem-tra" | "thong-bao" | "thao-luan"

const LABEL_CLASS =
  "hidden lg:inline font-['Be_Vietnam_Pro'] font-normal text-[14px] leading-[22px]"

const getItemClass = (isActive: boolean) =>
  `flex flex-col lg:flex-row items-center justify-center lg:justify-start px-0 lg:px-3 py-0 lg:py-2 gap-0 lg:gap-3 w-[76.39px] lg:w-full h-16 lg:h-[38px] lg:rounded-xl transition-colors cursor-pointer ${

      : "text-[#464555] dark:text-gray-300 hover:bg-[#E2E7FF]/60 dark:hover:bg-gray-800 hover:text-[#3525CD] dark:hover:text-white"
  }`

const getIconWrapperClass = (isActive: boolean) =>
  `flex items-center justify-center w-[45px] h-[45px] lg:w-5 lg:h-5 shrink-0 rounded-full lg:rounded-none transition-all ${
    isActive ? "bg-[#6750A3] text-white shadow-sm" : "bg-transparent text-[#464555] dark:text-gray-300"
  }`

function getActiveFromPath(pathname: string): ActiveItem {
  if (pathname.startsWith("/discuss")) return "thao-luan"
  if (pathname.startsWith("/my-courses")) return "khoa-hoc"
  return "trang-chu"
}

export default function Sidebar({ onOpenNotification, onCloseNotification }: SidebarProps) {
  const { t } = useTranslation()
  const location = useLocation()
  const unreadCountQuery = useGetUnreadNotificationCount(Boolean(accessTokenStorage.getAccessToken()))
  const unreadCount = unreadCountQuery.data?.unread ?? 0
  const unreadLabel = unreadCount > 99 ? "99+" : unreadCount

  // Má»¥c Ä‘Æ°á»£c chá»n thá»§ cÃ´ng (thÃ´ng bÃ¡o, bÃ i kiá»ƒm tra) - chá»‰ cÃ³ hiá»‡u lá»±c trong láº§n Ä‘iá»u hÆ°á»›ng hiá»‡n táº¡i
  const [selectedItem, setSelectedItem] = useState<{ item: ActiveItem; locationKey: string } | null>(null)
  const activeItem: ActiveItem =
    selectedItem?.locationKey === location.key
      ? selectedItem.item
      : getActiveFromPath(location.pathname)

  const selectItem = (item: ActiveItem) => setSelectedItem({ item, locationKey: location.key })

  // DÃ¹ng cho cÃ¡c link Ä‘iá»u hÆ°á»›ng tháº­t: xoÃ¡ lá»±a chá»n thá»§ cÃ´ng vÃ  Ä‘Ã³ng panel thÃ´ng bÃ¡o
  const handleNavigate = () => {
    setSelectedItem(null)
    onCloseNotification?.()
  }

  return (
    <aside className="fixed bottom-0 left-0 right-0 z-40 flex flex-col lg:absolute lg:top-16 lg:h-[calc(100vh-64px)] lg:w-64 bg-[#F2F3FF] dark:bg-gray-900 border-t lg:border-t-0 lg:border-r border-[#E2E7FF] dark:border-gray-700">

        {/* 1. Trang chá»§ */}

          <span className={LABEL_CLASS}>{t("nav.my_courses", "KhoÃ¡ há»c cá»§a tÃ´i")}</span>
        </Link>

            selectItem("bai-kiem-tra")
            onCloseNotification?.()
          }}

import { useState } from 'react'
import { FontAwesomeIcon } from '@fortawesome/react-fontawesome'
import { faMoon, faSun } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'

type Theme = 'light' | 'dark'
const STORAGE_KEY = 'theme'

// Äá»“ng bá»™ vá»›i class Ä‘Ã£ Ä‘Æ°á»£c script trong index.html gáº¯n sáºµn
const getCurrentTheme = (): Theme =>
  document.documentElement.classList.contains('dark') ? 'dark' : 'light'

interface Props {
  className?: string
}

export default function ThemeToggle({ className = '' }: Props) {
  const [theme, setTheme] = useState<Theme>(getCurrentTheme)

  const toggle = () => {
    const next: Theme = theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark'
    document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark', next === 'dark')
    localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, next)
    setTheme(next)
  }

  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      onClick={toggle}
      className={`grid size-16 place-items-center rounded-full border border-border bg-surface text-fg-muted transition hover:bg-primary-soft hover:text-primary ${className}`}
    >
      {theme === 'dark' ? <FontAwesomeIcon icon={faSun} /> : <FontAwesomeIcon icon={faMoon} />}
    </button>
  )
}

import {
  createContext,
  useCallback,
  useContext,
  useMemo,
  useRef,
  useState,
  type ReactNode,
} from 'react'
import { FontAwesomeIcon } from '@fortawesome/react-fontawesome'
import {
  faCircleCheck,
  faCircleExclamation,
  faCircleInfo,
  faXmark,
} from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'

type ToastType = 'success' | 'error' | 'info'

interface ToastItem {
  id: number
  type: ToastType
  message: string
}

interface ToastApi {
  show: (message: string, type?: ToastType, duration?: number) => void
  success: (message: string, duration?: number) => void
  error: (message: string, duration?: number) => void
  info: (message: string, duration?: number) => void
}

const ToastContext = createContext<ToastApi | null>(null)

const styles: Record<ToastType, { icon: typeof faCircleInfo; color: string }> = {
  success: { icon: faCircleCheck, color: 'text-emerald-500' },
  error: { icon: faCircleExclamation, color: 'text-danger' },
  info: { icon: faCircleInfo, color: 'text-primary' },
}

export function ToastProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const [toasts, setToasts] = useState<ToastItem[]>([])
  const idRef = useRef(0)

  const remove = useCallback((id: number) => {
    setToasts((list) => list.filter((t) => t.id !== id))
  }, [])

  const show = useCallback(
    (message: string, type: ToastType = 'info', duration = 4000) => {
      const id = ++idRef.current
      setToasts((list) => [...list, { id, type, message }])
      if (duration > 0) setTimeout(() => remove(id), duration)
    },
    [remove],
  )

  const api = useMemo<ToastApi>(
    () => ({
      show,
      success: (m, d) => show(m, 'success', d),
      error: (m, d) => show(m, 'error', d),
      info: (m, d) => show(m, 'info', d),
    }),
    [show],
  )

  return (
    <ToastContext.Provider value={api}>
      {children}
      <div className="pointer-events-none fixed top-4 right-4 z-50 flex w-[calc(100%-2rem)] max-w-sm flex-col gap-2">
        {toasts.map((t) => (
          <div
            key={t.id}
            role={t.type === 'error' ? 'alert' : 'status'}
            className="pointer-events-auto flex items-start gap-3 rounded-xl border border-border bg-surface p-3 text-sm text-fg shadow-lg"
          >
            <FontAwesomeIcon
              icon={styles[t.type].icon}
              className={`mt-0.5 ${styles[t.type].color}`}
            />
            <p className="flex-1 break-words">{t.message}</p>
            <button
              type="button"
              onClick={() => remove(t.id)}
              aria-label="Close"
              className="text-fg-subtle hover:text-fg"
            >
              <FontAwesomeIcon icon={faXmark} />
            </button>
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
    </ToastContext.Provider>
  )
}

export function useToast() {
  const ctx = useContext(ToastContext)
  if (!ctx) throw new Error('useToast must be used inside <ToastProvider>')
  return ctx
}

const ACCESS_TOKEN_KEY = 'access_token'
const USER_ID_KEY = 'user_id'

export const accessTokenStorage = {
  getAccessToken: () => localStorage.getItem(ACCESS_TOKEN_KEY),
  setAccessToken: (token: string) => localStorage.setItem(ACCESS_TOKEN_KEY, token),
  getUserId: () => {
    const userId = Number(localStorage.getItem(USER_ID_KEY))
    return Number.isInteger(userId) && userId > 0 ? userId : null
  },
  setUserId: (userId: number) => localStorage.setItem(USER_ID_KEY, String(userId)),
  clearAccessToken: () => {
    localStorage.removeItem(ACCESS_TOKEN_KEY)
    localStorage.removeItem(USER_ID_KEY)
  },
}

import axios, { AxiosError, type AxiosResponse } from 'axios'

import { accessTokenStorage } from './accessTokenStorage'

interface ApiEnvelope<T = unknown> {
  success?: boolean
  data?: T
  error_message?: string
  error_code?: string | number
}

const LOGIN_PATH_FE = '/login'
const PUBLIC_PATHS_BE = ["/health", "/auth/login", "/auth/register", "/error"];

const isPublicRequest = (url?: string) =>
  !!url && PUBLIC_PATHS_BE.some((path) => url.includes(path))

const isTokenExpired = (token: string) => {
  try {
    const base64 = token.split('.')[1].replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/')
    const payload = JSON.parse(atob(base64))
    return typeof payload.exp === 'number' && payload.exp * 1000 <= Date.now()
  } catch {
    return false
  }
}

let onUnauthorized: (() => void) | null = null
export const setUnauthorizedHandler = (handler: () => void) => {
  onUnauthorized = handler
}

const redirectToLogin = () => {
  accessTokenStorage.clearAccessToken()
  if (window.location.pathname === LOGIN_PATH_FE) return
  if (onUnauthorized) onUnauthorized()
  else window.location.replace(LOGIN_PATH_FE)
}

export const api = axios.create({
  baseURL: `${import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL}/api`,
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  timeout: 15_000,
})

api.interceptors.request.use((config) => {
  if (isPublicRequest(config.url)) return config

  const token = accessTokenStorage.getAccessToken()

  if (!token || isTokenExpired(token)) {
    redirectToLogin()
    return Promise.reject(new axios.CanceledError('Unauthenticated'))
  }

  config.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`
  return config
})

api.interceptors.response.use(
  (response) => {
    const body = response.data as ApiEnvelope | undefined

    if (body && typeof body === 'object' && body.success === false) {
      return Promise.reject(
        new AxiosError(
          body.error_message || 'Request failed',
          body.error_code !== undefined ? String(body.error_code) : undefined,
          response.config,
          response.request,
          response,
        ),
      )
    }

    const result = body?.data !== undefined ? body.data : body
    return result as unknown as AxiosResponse
  },
  (error: AxiosError<ApiEnvelope>) => {
    if (axios.isCancel(error)) return Promise.reject(error)

    if (error.response?.status === 401 && !isPublicRequest(error.config?.url)) {
      redirectToLogin()
    }

    const serverMessage = error.response?.data?.error_message
    if (serverMessage) error.message = serverMessage

    return Promise.reject(error)
  },
)

export const getApi = <T>(path: string, params?: Record<string, unknown>) =>
  api.get(path, { params }) as unknown as Promise<T>

export const postApi = <T>(path: string, body?: unknown) =>
  api.post(path, body) as unknown as Promise<T>

export const putApi = <T>(path: string, body?: unknown) =>
  api.put(path, body) as unknown as Promise<T>

export const patchApi = <T>(path: string, body?: unknown) =>
  api.patch(path, body) as unknown as Promise<T>

export const deleteApi = <T>(path: string) =>
  api.delete(path) as unknown as Promise<T>
